Why these

### Numbers you can check

#### The formula is always shown

Every page states the arithmetic it uses, with a worked example, so you can check the answer yourself.

#### Any currency

Pay figures and conversions work in every currency your browser knows, with live mid-market rates and the rupee in lakh and crore style.

#### Private

Everything is calculated in your browser. The figures you type are never uploaded or stored.

About

### How to read the results

Each calculator shows its formula and a worked example on the page, so you can check the answer by hand. Pay figures are gross, before tax. The income tax tool names the financial years and slabs it uses, the loan tools state their formula, and the currency tools use public daily reference rates, not the rate a bank will give you. The guides explain the rules behind the numbers: how overtime is calculated, where the 2,080-hour year comes from, and how exchange-rate margins work. They are estimates for planning, not financial, tax or legal advice.

### How a paycheck is calculated

- Start with gross pay, the amount before anything is taken out.
- Subtract pre-tax deductions. Retirement contributions such as a 401(k) lower the pay your income tax is based on. Health premiums and similar benefits also lower the pay Social Security and Medicare are based on.
- Subtract the standard deduction to get taxable income ( $16,100 single, $32,200 married filing jointly, $24,150 head of household in 2026).
- Apply the tax brackets. Each rate applies only to the slice of income inside its bracket, not to all of it.
- Add Social Security and Medicare (together called FICA).
- Add state and local tax, then any after-tax deductions. What is left is take-home pay.

### 2026 federal income tax brackets

The rate applies to taxable income inside each range. These are the figures the IRS published for 2026 in Revenue Procedure 2025-32.
Rate Single or married filing separately Married filing jointly Head of household
10 % $0 to $12,400 $0 to $24,800 $0 to $17,700
12 % $12,400 to $50,400 $24,800 to $100,800 $17,700 to $67,450
22 % $50,400 to $105,700 $100,800 to $211,400 $67,450 to $105,700
24 % $105,700 to $201,775 $211,400 to $403,550 $105,700 to $201,750
32 % $201,775 to $256,225 $403,550 to $512,450 $201,750 to $256,200
35 % $256,225 to $640,600 $512,450 to $768,700 $256,200 to $640,600
37 % Over $640,600 Over $768,700 Over $640,600

### Social Security and Medicare

- Social Security: 6.2% of wages, up to $184,500 a year in 2026. Pay above that is not charged Social Security tax.
- Medicare: 1.45% of all wages, plus an extra 0.9% on wages above $200,000.
- Your employer pays a matching share on top. It does not come out of your check.

### State income tax

State rules differ, so this is the part to check against your own state. 9 states do not tax wages: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, Wyoming. 15 states charge one flat rate, and the calculator fills those in when you pick the state. The rest use graduated rates, so enter your own percentage. Many cities and counties add a local tax, which you can include in the same box.
State with a flat rate 2026 rate
Arizona 2.5 %
Colorado 4.4 %
Georgia 5.19 %
Idaho 5.3 %
Illinois 4.95 %
Indiana 2.95 %
Iowa 3.8 %
Kentucky 3.5 %
Louisiana 3 %
Michigan 4.25 %
Mississippi 4 %
North Carolina 3.99 %
Ohio 2.75 %
Pennsylvania 3.07 %
Utah 4.5 %

### What this estimate leaves out

Real withholding depends on the Form W-4 you gave your employer and on IRS Publication 15-T, so a paycheck can differ from this estimate by a few dollars. The calculator does not include the child tax credit or other credits, extra income, overtime or bonuses, state standard deductions or exemptions, or payroll taxes some states add (such as state disability insurance). Use it to plan, and your pay stub for the exact figure.

### Sources

- IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32 (brackets and standard deduction), checked 4 November 2026.
- Social Security Administration: contribution and benefit base, checked 4 November 2026.
- IRS Topic 751: Social Security and Medicare withholding rates.
- Tax Foundation: state income tax rates for 2026, checked 4 November 2026.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I calculate my paycheck after taxes?
Take your gross pay, subtract pre-tax deductions such as a 401(k), subtract the standard deduction to find taxable income, and apply the federal brackets. Then add Social Security (6.2%) and Medicare (1.45%), state and local tax, and any after-tax deductions. What remains is take-home pay. This calculator does all of it from your salary.

How much is taken out of a paycheck?
For a single filer earning $60,000, about 16 percent goes to federal tax, Social Security and Medicare combined, before any state tax. The share rises with income because the brackets are marginal, and falls with pre-tax deductions such as a 401(k).

Why is my real paycheck different from the estimate?
Employers withhold using your Form W-4 and the IRS payroll method in Publication 15-T, not your final tax bill. A different W-4, extra income, credits, local taxes or benefits not entered here all change the real figure. Your pay stub is the exact number.

Does a 401(k) contribution lower my tax?
A traditional 401(k) contribution lowers the pay your income tax is based on, so your take-home pay falls by less than the amount you contribute. It does not lower Social Security or Medicare tax. A Roth 401(k) is taken after tax and does not lower income tax today.

Which states have no income tax?
Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington and Wyoming do not tax wages. Pick one of them in the calculator and the state tax is set to zero.

Is bonus or overtime pay taxed differently?
Not at a special rate. They are added to your income and taxed through the same brackets, but employers often withhold a flat percentage from a bonus, which can make the check look smaller than the final tax owed.

### How an hourly wage becomes take-home pay

Gross pay = hourly rate x hours per week x 52. The calculator treats that as your yearly income, works out the tax on it, and divides by the number of paychecks. A $20 hourly rate at 40 hours is $41,600 a year; at 25 hours it is $26,000.

### Take-home pay by hourly rate

Weekly take-home at 40 hours for a single filer using the standard deduction, with no state tax, no retirement contributions and no other deductions. The figures are computed with the same tax tables as the calculator above.
Hourly rate Gross per year Federal tax per year Social Security + Medicare Take-home per week
$15.00 $31,200 $1,564 $2,387 $524.02
$20.00 $41,600 $2,812 $3,182 $684.72
$25.00 $52,000 $4,060 $3,978 $845.42
$30.00 $62,400 $5,308 $4,774 $1,006.12
$40.00 $83,200 $9,474 $6,365 $1,295.41

### Part-time hours at $20 an hour

Fewer hours lower gross pay and also the share that goes to income tax, because less of the year&#x27;s pay is above the standard deduction. Social Security and Medicare apply from the first dollar.
Hours a week Gross per week Federal tax per week Take-home per week Take-home as a share of gross
20 hours $400.00 $9.04 $360.36 90.1 %
30 hours $600.00 $30.08 $524.02 87.3 %
40 hours $800.00 $54.08 $684.72 85.6 %

### A week with overtime

The calculator assumes the same hours every week. For a week with overtime, find the gross pay first. At $20 an hour, 45 hours with overtime after 40 at time and a half is $800.00 for the first 40 hours plus $150.00 for 5 overtime hours, or $950.00 gross. If every week were like that one, take-home would be about $805.25 a week on the same assumptions. Use the overtime pay calculator to work out other weeks.

### Minimum wage workers and income tax

The federal minimum wage is $7.25 an hour. At 40 hours for 52 weeks that is $15,080 a year, below the $16,100 standard deduction for a single filer, so the federal income tax in this model is $0. Social Security and Medicare still apply to every dollar. Many states and cities set a higher minimum wage and some have their own income tax, so check your own. Source: 29 U.S.C. 206, checked 16 November 2026.

### How a paycheck is calculated

- Start with gross pay, the amount before anything is taken out.
- Subtract pre-tax deductions. Retirement contributions such as a 401(k) lower the pay your income tax is based on. Health premiums and similar benefits also lower the pay Social Security and Medicare are based on.
- Subtract the standard deduction to get taxable income ( $16,100 single, $32,200 married filing jointly, $24,150 head of household in 2026).
- Apply the tax brackets. Each rate applies only to the slice of income inside its bracket, not to all of it.
- Add Social Security and Medicare (together called FICA).
- Add state and local tax, then any after-tax deductions. What is left is take-home pay.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I calculate an hourly paycheck?
Multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work in a week, then by 52 for the year. Subtract pre-tax deductions and the standard deduction, apply the federal brackets, and add Social Security, Medicare and state tax. Divide by your number of paychecks for the amount per check.

How much is $20 an hour after taxes?
At 40 hours a week, $20 an hour is $41,600 a year before tax. For a single filer with no state tax and no other deductions, take-home pay comes to about $35,606 a year, or $684.72 a week. Enter your own details above for your filing status and state.

Does this include overtime?
No. It assumes the same hours every week. To estimate a week with overtime, work out the gross pay with the overtime calculator, then use the average hours per week here for a rough take-home figure. A 45-hour week at $20 with time and a half is $950.00 gross.

Why does my hourly paycheck change from week to week?
Hours change, and the tax withheld changes with them. Employers also annualise each paycheck to decide the withholding, so a larger check can look taxed more heavily even though the final tax is calculated on the whole year.

How much is take-home pay at 30 hours a week?
At $20 an hour and 30 hours a week, gross pay is $31,200 a year, and take-home is about $27,249 a year ($524.02 a week) for a single filer with no state tax.

Do part-time workers pay Social Security and Medicare?
Yes. Social Security (6.2%) and Medicare (1.45%) are charged on every dollar of wages. Income tax may be zero if your yearly pay stays under the standard deduction.

# Pay Raise Calculator: New Salary or Hourly Pay

## Pay Raise Calculator

Enter your current pay and the raise to see your new pay, or enter your old and new pay to find the percent raise. Works for salary and hourly wages.

Current pay ( $)
Pay basis per year per hour per month per week
Currency USD INR EUR GBP AUD CAD AED SGD JPY CHF

#### If you get this raise every year

Year Pay per year
Year 1 $61,800
Year 2 $63,654
Year 3 $65,564
Year 4 $67,531

### How to calculate a pay raise

Three modes cover the usual questions:

- Raise by %: new pay = current pay x (1 + raise / 100). It also shows what your pay becomes if you get the same percentage raise each year for five years, compounding.
- Raise by amount: new pay = current pay + raise. The calculator reports the raise as a percentage of your current pay.
- Find the % raise: raise % = (new pay - current pay) / current pay x 100. A negative result means a pay cut.
Worked example: a 3% raise on $60,000. $60,000 x 1.03 = $61,800, an increase of $1,800 a year. Going the other way, from $60,000 to $62,500 is a 4.17% raise.

### What a raise is worth on $60,000

The same starting salary at different raise percentages, with the extra amount per month and per week, before tax.
Raise New yearly pay Extra per year Extra per month Extra per week
1 % $60,600 $600 $50.00 $11.54
2 % $61,200 $1,200 $100.00 $23.08
3 % $61,800 $1,800 $150.00 $34.62
4 % $62,400 $2,400 $200.00 $46.15
5 % $63,000 $3,000 $250.00 $57.69
7 % $64,200 $4,200 $350.00 $80.77
10 % $66,000 $6,000 $500.00 $115.38

### A raise every year compounds

A percentage raise is applied to last year&#x27;s pay, so the gains build on each other. Five years of 3% raises on $60,000:
After Yearly pay Total gain so far
Year 1 $61,800 $1,800
Year 2 $63,654 $3,654
Year 3 $65,564 $5,564
Year 4 $67,531 $7,531
Year 5 $69,556 $9,556

### Is your raise a real raise?

Prices change too, so a raise that matches the rise in prices leaves your buying power unchanged. The real change is (1 + raise) / (1 + inflation) - 1. The inflation rates below are examples to show the arithmetic, not forecasts; use the figure that applies to you.
Your raise If prices rise 2 % If prices rise 3 % If prices rise 4 % If prices rise 5 %
2 % 0% -0.97% -1.92% -2.86%
3 % 0.98% 0% -0.96% -1.9%
4 % 1.96% 0.97% 0% -0.95%
5 % 2.94% 1.94% 0.96% 0%
7 % 4.9% 3.88% 2.88% 1.9%

### Getting back after a pay cut

A percentage cut and the same percentage raise do not cancel out, because the raise applies to the lower pay.
Pay cut Pay after the cut Raise needed to get back
5 % $57,000 5.26%
10 % $54,000 11.11%
15 % $51,000 17.65%
20 % $48,000 25%

### What this calculator leaves out

It works on gross pay. A raise adds less to take-home pay than to gross pay because tax and payroll deductions apply to it. To see the per-period effect, convert the new figure with the salary calculator, and to see the after-tax effect use the paycheck calculator with the old and new salary.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I calculate a percentage raise?
Multiply your current pay by 1 plus the raise as a decimal. A 3% raise on $50,000 is $50,000 x 1.03 = $51,500, an increase of $1,500.

How do I find what percent raise I got?
Subtract your old pay from your new pay, divide by your old pay, and multiply by 100. Going from $50,000 to $55,000 is ($55,000 - $50,000) / $50,000 x 100 = 10%.

What percent is a $5,000 raise?
It depends on the starting pay. On $50,000 it is 10%; on $80,000 it is 6.25%; on $100,000 it is 5%.

Does a raise work the same for hourly pay?
Yes. The percentage is applied to the rate, so a 4% raise on $20.00 an hour gives $20.80 an hour. Multiply by your weekly hours to see the effect on a paycheck: at 40 hours that is $32.00 more a week.

How much more per paycheck is a raise?
Divide the yearly increase by the number of paychecks. A raise from $60,000 to $61,800 adds $69.23 to each bi-weekly check and $34.62 a week, before tax.

Is the result before or after tax?
Before. The calculator works on gross pay. Your take-home increase will be smaller because income tax and payroll deductions apply to the extra pay. The paycheck calculator shows the after-tax difference.

How big does a raise need to be to keep up with inflation?
At least as large as the rate prices are rising. If prices rise 3% and your pay rises 3%, your buying power is unchanged. A raise of 2% when prices rise 3% is a real change of -0.97%, which is a small pay cut in buying power.

If my pay was cut, what raise gets me back?
More than the size of the cut, because the raise applies to a smaller number. After a 10% cut you need a 11.11% raise to get back to where you were.

What is a compounding raise?
The same percentage raise each year, each applied to the previous year&#x27;s pay. Three years of 3% on $60,000 gives $65,564, which is more than three separate $1,800 increases would give ($65,400).

Pay amount ( $)

### How the conversion works

Every conversion goes through annual pay. The calculator turns your figure into a year, then divides the year into the period you want. With a schedule of H hours a week, D days a week and W weeks a year:
From Annual pay Back to this period
Hourly rate x H x W annual / (H x W)
Daily rate x D x W annual / (D x W)
Weekly rate x W annual / W
Bi-weekly rate x W / 2 annual / (W / 2)
Semi-monthly rate x 24 annual / 24
Monthly rate x 12 annual / 12
Quarterly rate x 4 annual / 4

### Example: a $60,000 salary in every period

At 40 hours a week, 5 days a week and 52 weeks a year, a $60,000 salary is the same pay written different ways:
Period Pay Count in a year
Hourly $28.85 2,080 hours
Daily $230.77 260 days
Weekly $1,153.85 52 paychecks
Bi-weekly $2,307.69 26 paychecks
Semi-monthly $2,500.00 24 paychecks
Monthly $5,000.00 12 paychecks
Quarterly $15,000.00 4 payments
A bi-weekly check is smaller than a semi-monthly one because there are more of them. A bi-weekly schedule usually has two months a year with three paychecks; a semi-monthly schedule never does. The US Office of Personnel Management notes that there are usually 26 bi-weekly pay dates a year, but that some calendar years have 27.

### What this calculator leaves out

It gives gross pay for a steady schedule. It does not include overtime, bonuses, commissions or tips, and it does not take off tax or deductions. ### Frequently asked questions

How do I convert hourly pay to annual salary?
Multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work in a week and by the weeks you work in a year. At 40 hours and 52 weeks that is 2,080 hours, so $25 an hour is $52,000 a year.

How do I convert an annual salary to monthly pay?
Divide by 12. A $60,000 salary is $5,000.00 a month. Do not multiply by 4 weeks; a year has 52 weeks, which is about 4.33 a month.

Why is monthly pay not just four weeks of pay?
A year has 52 weeks, which is about 4.33 weeks a month, not 4. At $25 an hour, four weeks is $4,000.00, but the true monthly figure is $4,333.33.

What is the difference between bi-weekly and semi-monthly?
Bi-weekly means every two weeks, which is 26 paychecks a year. Semi-monthly means twice a month, which is 24. A $60,000 salary pays $2,307.69 per bi-weekly check and $2,500.00 per semi-monthly check. The yearly total is the same.

Why do some years have 27 pay dates?
With bi-weekly pay there are usually 26 pay dates a year, but over several years some calendar years have 27, because 52 weeks is 364 days and a year has 365 or 366. The US Office of Personnel Management notes this for federal pay.

How do I convert daily pay to annual pay?
Multiply the daily rate by the days you work in a week and by the weeks in a year. At $230.77 a day, five days a week for 52 weeks, that is $60,000.

Can I change the hours or weeks?
Yes. Edit hours per week, days per week and weeks per year. Use fewer weeks if you take unpaid time off, and fewer hours for part-time work. Paid holidays and paid leave count as worked.

Does this include overtime or bonuses?
No. It assumes the same pay every period. Use the overtime pay calculator to add hours at a higher rate, and add bonuses to the annual figure yourself.

Is this before or after tax?
Before. These are gross figures. For take-home pay after tax, use the paycheck calculator.

### How to convert hourly pay to a yearly salary

Annual salary = hourly rate x hours per week x weeks per year. The standard full-time year is 40 hours x 52 weeks = 2,080 hours, which is the default here. Divide the annual figure by 12 for monthly pay, by 26 for bi-weekly pay, or by 52 for weekly pay.

- Find your hours. Use the hours you are paid for in a typical week, 40 for full time.
- Multiply by the weeks you are paid. 52 if you are paid all year, including paid holidays and leave.
- Multiply by your hourly rate. That is the annual salary before tax.
Worked example: $25 an hour, 40 hours, 52 weeks. 40 x 52 = 2,080 hours, and 2,080 x $25 = $52,000 a year. That is $4,333.33 a month, $2,000.00 every two weeks and $1,000.00 a week.

### Hourly pay versus salary

An hourly wage pays for every hour you work, including overtime at a higher rate where the law requires it. A salary is a fixed amount per year, so the real value of a salary depends on how many hours the job takes. When you compare an hourly offer with a salaried one, convert the salary to hourly with the salary to hourly calculator using the hours the job really takes.

### What this calculator leaves out

It assumes the same hours every week. It does not add overtime, shift differentials, bonuses or tips, and it does not take off tax. For a week with overtime, use the overtime pay calculator; for take-home pay, use the hourly paycheck calculator. To see the same pay in every period at once, use the salary calculator.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I turn an hourly wage into a salary?
Multiply the hourly rate by hours per week and by 52. Full-time at 40 hours is 2,080 hours a year, so $25 an hour is $25 x 2,080 = $52,000.

How much is $15 an hour per year?
$31,200 a year at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks, which is $2,600.00 a month before tax.

How much is $20 an hour per year?
$41,600 a year at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks, or $3,466.67 a month before tax.

How much is $30 an hour per year?
$62,400 a year at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks, or $5,200.00 a month before tax.

How do I calculate salary for part-time hours?
Use your real weekly hours. At $18 an hour and 30 hours a week, annual pay is $18 x 30 x 52 = $28,080.

What if I do not work all 52 weeks?
Change weeks per year. At $25 an hour, 40 hours a week and 50 paid weeks, annual pay is $25 x 40 x 50 = $50,000. Paid vacation and holidays count as worked weeks; unpaid time off does not.

How do I get monthly pay from an hourly wage?
Work out the annual figure first, then divide by 12. $25 an hour is $52,000 a year, so $4,333.33 a month, not four weeks of pay, because a year has more than 48 weeks.

Does this include overtime?
No. It assumes the same hours every week. Use the overtime pay calculator to add hours paid at a higher rate.

Is the answer before tax?
Yes. It is gross pay before income tax and other deductions. The hourly paycheck calculator shows take-home pay.

### How to convert a salary to an hourly rate

Hourly pay = annual salary / (hours per week x weeks per year). With the standard 2,080-hour year (40 hours x 52 weeks), divide your salary by 2,080.

- Get the yearly figure. If you know a monthly salary, multiply by 12.
- Count your yearly hours. Hours per week times weeks per year: 40 x 52 = 2,080.
- Divide. Salary divided by yearly hours is the hourly rate.
Worked example: $60,000 / 2,080 = $28.85 an hour. That is $230.77 a day and $1,153.85 a week. Our guide to the 2,080-hour rule explains where the number comes from.

### Your real hourly rate depends on your real hours

A salary does not change when you work extra hours, so every extra hour lowers your effective hourly rate. This is what a $60,000 and a $90,000 salary are worth per hour at different weekly hours.
Hours a week $60,000 a year $90,000 a year Rate vs a 40-hour week
40 hours $28.85 $43.27 baseline

50 hours $23.08 $34.62 -20%
55 hours $20.98 $31.47 -27.3%

Put your real hours in the calculator before comparing a salary with an hourly offer. If an hourly job pays overtime and the salaried one does not, the gap is larger than the plain rates suggest; use the overtime pay calculator to price the hourly week.

### 2,080 hours or 2,087 hours?

2,080 is 40 hours x 52 weeks and is the usual convention. A calendar year is 365 or 366 days, which is a little more than 52 weeks, so the US federal pay system divides annual pay by 2,087 hours instead and rounds each hourly rate to the nearest cent. The Office of Personnel Management explains that 2,087 is the average number of work hours in a calendar year over a 28-year cycle. The difference is about 0.34%, or $0.10 an hour on a $60,000 salary. If your employer states a divisor, set weeks per year to match it.

### What this calculator leaves out

It gives gross pay and assumes the same hours every week. It does not model unpaid leave, bonuses or benefits, and it does not take off tax. To go the other way, use the hourly to salary calculator. For take-home pay, use the paycheck calculator.

- US Office of Personnel Management: computing hourly rates of pay using the 2,087-hour divisor, checked 16 November 2026.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I convert salary to hourly?
Divide annual salary by the hours you work in a year. For a standard full-time year that is 40 x 52 = 2,080 hours, so $60,000 a year is $60,000 / 2,080 = $28.85 an hour.

How do I convert a monthly salary to hourly?
Multiply the monthly amount by 12 to get the annual figure, then divide by 2,080. $5,000 a month is $60,000 a year, or $28.85 an hour.

How much is a $50,000 salary per hour?
$24.04 an hour at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks. At 45 hours a week it is $21.37.

How much is a $100,000 salary per hour?
$48.08 an hour at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks, or $38.46 an hour if the job regularly takes 50 hours.

What if I work more than 40 hours a week?
Set hours per week to what you really work. A $60,000 salary at 50 hours a week is $60,000 / (50 x 52) = $23.08 an hour, well below the $28.85 you get at 40 hours.

Why do some people use 2,087 hours?
The US federal pay system divides annual pay by 2,087 hours, the average number of work hours in a calendar year over a 28-year cycle, because a calendar year is 365 or 366 days, not exactly 52 weeks. 2,080 is the common convention elsewhere. The two differ by about 0.34%: on $60,000 that is $28.85 against $28.75.

Do paid holidays and vacation count as hours?
Yes. If you are paid for them, they are part of the salary, so keep weeks per year at 52. Reduce the weeks only for unpaid time off.

Is a salaried job paid for overtime?
Not automatically. A salaried job that is exempt from overtime pays the same however many hours you work. A salaried job that is not exempt is owed overtime. The guide to overtime pay explains the difference.

Is the hourly figure before tax?
Yes. It is gross pay.

# Overtime Pay Calculator: Weekly Pay with Overtime

## Overtime Pay Calculator

Enter your hourly rate and the hours you worked this week to see regular pay, overtime pay and the total. Change the threshold or multiplier for your state or contract.

Overtime multiplier 1.5x (time and a half) 2x (double time) 2.5x (double time and a half)

Total pay for the week $950.00
Overtime rate $30.00 /hr
Overtime pay $150.00

Part of the week Hours Pay
Regular hours at $20.00 40 $800.00
Overtime hours at $30.00 5 $150.00
Gross pay, before taxes and deductions.

### What overtime pay is

Overtime pay is the higher rate paid for hours beyond a weekly limit. In the US the usual limit is 40 hours in a workweek and the usual rate is one and a half times your regular hourly rate, called time and a half.
Weekly pay = regular hours x rate + overtime hours x rate x multiplier. Regular hours are the hours up to the threshold (40 by default). Overtime hours are everything beyond it. Time and a half uses a multiplier of 1.5 and double time uses 2.

### How to calculate overtime pay

- Split the week. Hours up to 40 are regular hours. Hours past 40 are overtime hours.
- Pay regular hours at your rate. 40 hours at $20 is $800.
- Pay overtime hours at the higher rate. $20 x 1.5 = $30, so each overtime hour pays $30.
- Add them. The two parts make the week&#x27;s gross pay.
Worked example: 45 hours at $20. Regular pay is 40 x $20 = $800.00. Overtime pay is 5 x $30 = $150.00. The week comes to $950.00. For the rate on its own, or a chart of common wages, use the time and a half calculator.

### Weekly pay at $20 an hour, by hours worked

The same rate, with overtime after 40 hours. The last column is the part of the week paid at time and a half.
Hours worked Pay at 1.5x Pay at 2x Overtime pay at 1.5x
40 $800.00 $800.00 $0.00
42 $860.00 $880.00 $60.00
45 $950.00 $1,000.00 $150.00
48 $1,040.00 $1,120.00 $240.00
50 $1,100.00 $1,200.00 $300.00
55 $1,250.00 $1,400.00 $450.00
60 $1,400.00 $1,600.00 $600.00

### The rules that decide whether you get overtime

The 40-hour week. The Fair Labor Standards Act says a covered employee may not work more than 40 hours in a workweek unless the extra hours are paid at “not less than one and one-half times the regular rate”.
Each week stands alone. The Act uses a single workweek as its standard and does not allow hours to be averaged over two or more weeks. A 30-hour week followed by a 50-hour week has 10 overtime hours in the second week.
The workweek. It is a fixed, regularly recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods). It may begin on any day and at any hour, and once set it stays fixed.
Exempt jobs. Some salaried jobs are exempt from overtime. For the federal executive, administrative and professional exemptions, the employee must be paid on a salary basis of at least $684 a week, which is $35,568 a year, and must also meet a duties test. A job title or a salary alone does not make someone exempt. The guide to overtime pay covers the exemptions in more detail.

### Overtime rules differ by state

The federal rule counts hours over 40 in a week. A state can go further. California, for example, requires:

- one and one-half times the regular rate for hours over 8 and up to 12 in a workday, and for the first 8 hours on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek; and
- double the regular rate for hours over 12 in a workday, and for hours over 8 on that seventh day.
At $20 an hour, a 10-hour day in California is 8 x $20 + 2 x $30 = $220.00 before any weekly overtime. Other states have their own rules and exceptions, so check your state labor department. To model a daily rule here, set the threshold to the daily limit and enter that day&#x27;s hours.

### When a bonus changes your overtime rate

Overtime is based on your regular rate, which is your total pay for the week divided by the hours worked, not always the base wage. A bonus promised in advance, such as an attendance or production bonus, counts towards it. A bonus left entirely to the employer&#x27;s discretion, in both whether and how much, does not.
The example in the federal regulations: a worker paid $12 an hour works 46 hours and earns a $46 production bonus. Straight-time pay is 46 x $12 = $552. Adding the bonus gives $598, and dividing by 46 hours gives a regular rate of $13.00. The 6 overtime hours earn an extra half of that rate: 6 x $6.50 = $39.00. The week&#x27;s total is $637. This calculator does not do that step for you; it uses the single rate you type in.

### What this calculator leaves out

It works on gross pay and one rate. It does not take off tax, handle two pay rates in the same week, add shift differentials or bonuses to the regular rate, or apply state daily overtime on its own. Treat the result as an estimate and check your payslip. For take-home pay, use the hourly paycheck calculator, and to turn a wage into a yearly figure use the hourly to salary calculator.

### Sources

- 29 U.S.C. 207, maximum hours (40 hours, one and one-half times the regular rate), checked 16 November 2026.
- 29 CFR 778.104, each workweek stands alone (no averaging), checked 16 November 2026.
- 29 CFR 778.105, determining the workweek (168 hours), checked 16 November 2026.
- 29 CFR 778.110, hourly rate and bonus (the bonus example) and 778.211, discretionary bonuses, checked 16 November 2026.
- 29 CFR 541.600, amount of salary required ($684 a week), checked 16 November 2026.
- California Department of Industrial Relations: overtime, checked 16 November 2026.

### Frequently asked questions

How is overtime pay calculated?
Pay the regular rate for hours up to the overtime threshold, and the regular rate times the multiplier for hours beyond it. At $20 an hour, 45 hours with time and a half is 40 x $20 + 5 x $30 = $950.00.

How do I calculate overtime for a 50-hour week?
At $15 an hour: 40 hours x $15 = $600, plus 10 hours x $22.50 = $225, which is $825.00. If your employer pays double time instead, the 10 hours are worth $300 and the week is $900.00.

When does overtime start?
Under the federal Fair Labor Standards Act, a covered employee must be paid at least one and one-half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek. Some states add their own rules, such as California, which also counts hours over 8 in a workday.

Does the 40-hour rule average across two weeks?
No. The federal rule takes a single workweek as its standard and does not allow averaging over two or more weeks. If you work 30 hours one week and 50 the next, you are owed overtime for the 10 hours in the second week, even though the two weeks average 40.

What counts as a workweek?
A fixed, regularly recurring period of 168 hours: seven consecutive 24-hour periods. It does not have to be a calendar week and can start on any day and hour. Once your employer sets the start, it stays fixed.

Are salaried employees entitled to overtime?
It depends on whether the job is exempt, which turns on duties and pay, not on being paid a salary. For the federal white-collar exemptions the regulation currently sets a minimum salary of $684 a week ($35,568 a year), and the duties test must also be met. A salaried employee who is non-exempt is owed overtime.

Is a bonus part of the rate overtime is based on?
Often, yes. The federal regular rate includes all pay for the work except specific exclusions. A bonus that is promised in advance, such as an attendance or production bonus, is part of it. A bonus left entirely to the employer&#x27;s discretion, in both whether it is paid and how much, is not. The example on this page works through one.

Is overtime taxed at a higher rate?
No. It is ordinary wages. A larger check can lead to more tax being withheld that period, but there is no special overtime tax rate. The time and a half calculator page covers a separate deduction for the extra half of overtime.

How do I enter double time or a daily rule?
Choose 2x in the multiplier list for double time. To model a daily rule, set the threshold to the daily limit (for example 8) and enter the hours for that one day, then add the days together.

### What time and a half means

Time and a half is your regular hourly rate multiplied by 1.5. The “time” is your normal rate and the “half” is an extra 50% on top. At $20 an hour that is $20 + $10 = $30 an hour.
Time and a half rate = regular hourly rate x 1.5

### How to calculate time and a half

- Find your regular hourly rate. If you are paid a salary, divide the yearly figure by 2,080 (40 hours x 52 weeks).
- Multiply it by 1.5. That is the rate for each overtime hour.
- Multiply by the overtime hours. That is your overtime pay before tax.
A worked week: 45 hours at $20 an hour, with overtime after 40. The first 40 hours pay 40 x $20 = $800. The 5 overtime hours pay 5 x $30 = $150. The week comes to $950, which is $50 more than 45 hours at the regular rate. To run a whole week like this, use the overtime pay calculator.

$28.00 $42.00 $56.00 $210.00 $420.00
$30.00 $45.00 $60.00 $225.00 $450.00
$35.00 $52.50 $70.00 $262.50 $525.00
$40.00 $60.00 $80.00 $300.00 $600.00
$50.00 $75.00 $100.00 $375.00 $750.00

### Time and a half from a salary

Divide the yearly salary by 2,080 to get an hourly rate, then multiply by 1.5. Change the 2,080 if your standard week is not 40 hours; the salary to hourly calculator does that for you.
Yearly salary Hourly rate (2,080 hours) Time and a half
$40,000 $19.23 $28.85
$50,000 $24.04 $36.06
$60,000 $28.85 $43.27
$75,000 $36.06 $54.09
$100,000 $48.08 $72.12
A salary does not by itself decide whether you are owed overtime. That depends on whether the job is exempt, which the guide to overtime pay explains.

### When the law requires time and a half

Federal rule. The Fair Labor Standards Act says a covered employee may not work more than 40 hours in a workweek unless the extra hours are paid at “not less than one and one-half times the regular rate”. The count is per workweek, not per day, and the federal rule does not add a premium for nights, weekends or holidays.
States can go further. California, for example, requires time and a half for hours over 8 and up to 12 in a workday and for the first 8 hours on the seventh day in a row of a workweek, and double time for hours over 12 in a workday and over 8 on that seventh day. Check your own state&#x27;s labor department for the rule that applies to you.
Employer policy. Many employers pay time and a half or double time for holidays or hard-to-fill shifts by choice or by contract. That is on top of what the law requires, so the terms are in your contract or handbook.

### Tax on the extra half

Overtime pay is ordinary wages. For tax years 2025 through 2028 the IRS allows a deduction for the pay that exceeds your regular rate, the “half” in time and a half, when that overtime is required by the Fair Labor Standards Act. The most you can deduct is $12,500 a year ($25,000 for joint filers), and it phases out above $150,000 of modified adjusted gross income ($300,000 for joint filers). At $20 an hour, $10 of each $30 overtime hour is the half that can count. It is claimed on your tax return, so read the IRS page below for who qualifies.

### What this calculator leaves out

It works on gross pay and one hourly rate. It does not take off tax, and it does not handle a regular rate that includes bonuses, shift differentials or two different pay rates in one week, which can raise the rate overtime is based on. For take-home pay after tax, use the hourly paycheck calculator.

### Sources

- 29 U.S.C. 207, maximum hours (the federal 40-hour, one-and-one-half-times rule), checked 15 November 2026.
- 29 U.S.C. 206, minimum wage ($7.25 an hour), checked 15 November 2026.
- California Department of Industrial Relations: overtime, checked 15 November 2026.
- IRS: tax deductions for working Americans and seniors (the overtime deduction), checked 15 November 2026.

### Frequently asked questions

What is time and a half?
Pay at 1.5 times your regular hourly rate. If you earn $20 an hour, time and a half is $20 x 1.5 = $30 an hour. The extra $10 is the &#x27;half&#x27;.

How do I calculate time and a half?
Multiply your hourly rate by 1.5. To find pay for overtime hours, multiply that rate by the hours: 5 hours at $30 is $150.

What is time and a half for $15 an hour?
$22.50 an hour ($15 x 1.5). At $18 an hour it is $27.00, and at $25 an hour it is $37.50. The chart on this page lists more rates.

Is time and a half the same as overtime?
Usually, but not always. Overtime is the hours beyond a limit, and time and a half is the usual rate paid for them. Some overtime is paid at double time, and some employers pay time and a half for hours that are not overtime, such as holidays.

What is double time?
Pay at twice your regular rate. At $20 an hour, double time is $40 an hour. It is set by employer policy, union contract or state law, not by the federal overtime rule.

Do I get time and a half for working holidays or weekends?
Not under federal law. The Fair Labor Standards Act only requires it for hours over 40 in a workweek. A premium for a holiday or weekend comes from your employer&#x27;s policy or contract, unless those hours also take you past 40 for the week.

Do salaried employees get time and a half?
Only if the job is non-exempt. A salary alone does not remove the right to overtime; the exemption depends on the duties of the job and the pay level. An exempt salaried employee is not owed overtime under the federal rule.

How do I calculate time and a half from a salary?
First convert the salary to an hourly rate (annual salary / 2,080 for a standard year), then multiply by 1.5. A $60,000 salary is $28.85 an hour, so time and a half is about $43.27.

Is time-and-a-half pay taxed differently?
It is ordinary wages, but for tax years 2025 through 2028 the IRS allows a deduction for the &#x27;half&#x27; portion of overtime required by the Fair Labor Standards Act, up to $12,500 a year ($25,000 for joint filers). The deduction phases out above $150,000 of modified adjusted gross income ($300,000 for joint filers).

## EMI Calculator

Year Principal paid Interest paid Balance remaining
Year 1 ₹1,65,830 ₹83,270 ₹8,34,170
Year 2 ₹1,81,386 ₹67,714 ₹6,52,784
Year 3 ₹1,98,401 ₹50,699 ₹4,54,383
Year 4 ₹2,17,013 ₹32,088 ₹2,37,370
Year 5 ₹2,37,370 ₹11,730 ₹0
Full month-by-month amortization schedule ( 60 months)

### What EMI means and how it is calculated

EMI stands for Equated Monthly Instalment: a fixed payment made every month until the loan is repaid. For a reducing-balance loan, the formula is:
EMI = [P x R x (1 + R)^N] / [(1 + R)^N - 1]

- P is the principal, the amount borrowed.
- R is the monthly interest rate: the annual rate divided by 12, then by 100.
- N is the number of monthly instalments (years x 12).
Each EMI pays the interest on the balance still owed that month, and the rest reduces the principal. Because the balance shrinks, the interest part shrinks and the principal part grows, even though the EMI stays the same. The calculator above shows this split for every year, and the full monthly table if you open it.

### How to calculate EMI step by step

- Convert the rate. 9 % a year is 9 / 12 / 100 = 0.0075 a month.
- Count the instalments. 5 years x 12 = 60 months.
- Apply the formula. For ₹10,00,000, the EMI is ₹20,758.
- Find the totals. ₹20,758 x 60 = ₹12,45,501 paid, so ₹2,45,501 is interest.

### How the tenure changes your EMI

The same ₹10,00,000 loan at 9 % over different terms. A longer term lowers the EMI but raises the interest.
Tenure Monthly EMI Total interest Total payment
1 year ₹87,451 ₹49,418 ₹10,49,418
2 years ₹45,685 ₹96,434 ₹10,96,434
3 years ₹31,800 ₹1,44,790 ₹11,44,790
5 years ₹20,758 ₹2,45,501 ₹12,45,501
7 years ₹16,089 ₹3,51,483 ₹13,51,483
10 years ₹12,668 ₹5,20,109 ₹15,20,109
15 years ₹10,143 ₹8,25,680 ₹18,25,680

### How the interest rate changes your EMI

The same ₹10,00,000 loan over 5 years at different rates.
Interest rate Monthly EMI Total interest EMI change vs 9 %
7 % ₹19,801 ₹1,88,072 -₹957
8 % ₹20,276 ₹2,16,584 -₹482
9 % ₹20,758 ₹2,45,501 baseline

11 % ₹21,742 ₹3,04,545 +₹984
12 % ₹22,244 ₹3,34,667 +₹1,486

### Flat rate and reducing balance are not the same

Some quotes, often for small or consumer loans, state a flat rate. Flat interest is charged on the full amount for the whole term, even though you repay part of it every month. A flat 9 % on ₹10,00,000 for 5 years is ₹10,00,000 x 9 % x 5 = ₹4,50,000 of interest, and an EMI of ( ₹10,00,000 + ₹4,50,000) / 60 = ₹24,167. The reducing-balance rate that gives that same EMI is about 15.7%. When you compare offers, ask which method the quoted rate uses.

### What a part-prepayment does

A lump sum paid towards the principal lowers the balance that interest is charged on. On the example loan, an extra ₹1,00,000 after the 12th EMI, with the EMI kept the same, clears the loan in 54 months instead of 60. Total interest falls from ₹2,45,501 to ₹2,05,431, a saving of ₹40,070. Your loan agreement says whether a prepayment charge applies and how a prepayment is applied (shorter tenure or lower EMI).

### What this leaves out

This is the standard EMI maths only. It does not include processing fees, insurance premiums some lenders bundle into the loan, GST on charges, or a floating-rate loan&#x27;s rate changing mid-term. Your lender&#x27;s sanction letter has the exact figures. For the loan size your income could support, see the loan eligibility calculator. For a specific loan type, use the home loan EMI or car loan EMI calculator.

### Frequently asked questions

What is the EMI formula?
EMI = [P x R x (1 + R)^N] / [(1 + R)^N - 1], where P is the loan amount, R is the monthly interest rate (annual rate divided by 12 and by 100), and N is the number of monthly instalments. It is the standard reducing-balance formula.

How do I calculate EMI for 10 lakh at 9% for 5 years?
P is 10,00,000, R is 9 / 12 / 100 = 0.0075 and N is 60. The EMI works out to ₹20,758 a month. Total payment is ₹12,45,501, of which ₹2,45,501 is interest.

Does the EMI stay the same every month?
Yes, for a fixed-rate reducing-balance loan the EMI is constant. What changes each month is the split inside it: early instalments are mostly interest and later ones are mostly principal, because interest is charged on the shrinking balance.

What is the difference between flat-rate and reducing-balance interest?
Reducing-balance interest, used by this calculator, charges interest only on the outstanding balance. Flat-rate interest charges on the original amount for the full term. A flat 9% on ₹10,00,000 for 5 years means ₹4,50,000 of interest and an EMI of ₹24,167, which is the same as a reducing-balance rate of about 15.7%.

How does a longer tenure change the EMI?
It lowers the EMI and raises the total interest. On ₹10,00,000 at 9%, 3 years gives an EMI of ₹31,800 and ₹1,44,790 of interest; 10 years gives ₹12,668 and ₹5,20,109.

How can I reduce my total interest?
A shorter tenure, a larger down payment (lower principal), a lower interest rate, or a part-prepayment during the loan each cut total interest, since each lowers either the balance interest is charged on or how long it is charged for.

How much does a part-prepayment save?
On ₹10,00,000 at 9% for 5 years, paying an extra ₹1,00,000 after the 12th EMI and keeping the EMI the same clears the loan in 54 months instead of 60 and cuts total interest from ₹2,45,501 to ₹2,05,431. Check your loan agreement for any prepayment charge first.

What happens to my EMI if the rate changes?
On a floating-rate loan a rate change can change the EMI or the tenure. Your loan agreement and your lender&#x27;s notice say which. Enter the new rate and the remaining months in the calculator to see the new EMI.

Does the EMI include processing fees or insurance?
No. The calculator shows interest and principal only. Processing fees, insurance and other charges are separate, and your sanction letter lists them.

### How a home loan EMI is worked out

A home loan EMI uses the standard reducing-balance formula: EMI = [P x R x (1 + R)^N] / [(1 + R)^N - 1]. P is the loan amount, R is the monthly rate (annual rate / 12 / 100) and N is the number of months. Home loans are usually the longest loan people take, so N is large (a 20-year loan is 240 months) and the total interest is large too.
Worked example: ₹35,00,000 at 8.5 % for 20 years ( 240 months). The EMI is ₹30,374 a month. Over the full term you pay ₹72,89,715, of which ₹37,89,715 is interest, about 1.08 times the amount borrowed.

### Why the early years are mostly interest

Interest is charged on the balance you still owe. At the start the balance is the whole loan, so most of each EMI is interest. On the example loan, year 1 pays ₹2,94,828 of interest and only ₹69,658 of principal, so the balance falls from ₹35,00,000 to ₹34,30,342. In year 20 the split reverses: ₹3,48,245 of principal and ₹16,241 of interest.

### How the tenure changes the cost

The same ₹35,00,000 at 8.5 % over different terms.
Tenure Monthly EMI Total interest Interest as a share of the loan
10 years ₹43,395 ₹17,07,399 49%
15 years ₹34,466 ₹27,03,859 77%
20 years ₹30,374 ₹37,89,715 108%
25 years ₹28,183 ₹49,54,884 142%

### How the down payment changes the loan

Enter the amount you borrow, not the property price. For an example property priced at ₹50,00,000, at 8.5 % over 20 years:
Down payment Down payment amount Loan amount Monthly EMI Total interest
10 % ₹5,00,000 ₹45,00,000 ₹39,052 ₹48,72,491

30 % ₹15,00,000 ₹35,00,000 ₹30,374 ₹37,89,715
40 % ₹20,00,000 ₹30,00,000 ₹26,035 ₹32,48,327

### If the rate changes during the loan

On a floating-rate loan the rate can move. On the example loan, a rise of one percentage point (to 9.5 %) takes the EMI from ₹30,374 to ₹32,625 if the 20 -year tenure stays. If you keep paying ₹30,374, the loan runs for about 309 months instead of 240. Enter the new rate and the months left in the calculator to see your own case.

### Tax on home loan interest

The Income Tax Department&#x27;s guidance for salaried individuals (assessment year 2026-27) lists the Section 24(b) deduction for interest paid on a housing loan. For a self-occupied property under the old tax regime, the limit is ₹2,00,000 a year for a loan taken on or after 1 April 1999 for construction or purchase. Its list for the new tax regime shows the deduction for let-out property only. Which regime is better depends on your whole tax position; the income tax calculator compares the two. Confirm current rules with the department or a tax adviser.

### What this leaves out

This estimate does not include processing fees, property or life insurance a lender bundles in, or a floating rate that changes during the loan. It does not model prepayments. For whether your income supports a given loan size, see the loan eligibility calculator. For a general loan, use the EMI calculator.

### Sources

- Income Tax Department: ITR guidance for salaried individuals, AY 2026-27 (Section 24(b) and the two regimes), checked 16 November 2026.

### Frequently asked questions

How is a home loan EMI calculated?
The same reducing-balance formula as any loan: EMI = [P x R x (1 + R)^N] / [(1 + R)^N - 1], where P is the loan amount, R is the monthly interest rate and N is the number of months. For ₹35,00,000 at 8.5% for 20 years, the EMI is ₹30,374.

What is the EMI for a 50 lakh home loan?
At 8.5% for 20 years, ₹50,00,000 gives an EMI of ₹43,391. At the same rate for 30 years it is ₹38,446. The rate is an example; use your lender&#x27;s rate.

How much of my EMI goes to interest in the early years?
A large share. On the ₹35,00,000 example, 81% of the first year&#x27;s payments is interest. The share falls as the balance falls, and by year 20 the loan is mostly principal.

Does the down payment affect the EMI?
Yes. A larger down payment lowers the principal you borrow, which lowers the EMI and the total interest, for the same rate and tenure. Enter the loan amount after your down payment, not the property price. On a ₹50,00,000 property, a 20% down payment leaves a ₹40,00,000 loan.

Should I choose a longer tenure for a lower EMI?
A longer tenure lowers the EMI but raises total interest. On ₹35,00,000 at 8.5%, 15 years costs ₹27,03,859 in interest and 25 years costs ₹49,54,884.

What happens if the interest rate rises by 1 percentage point?
On the example loan, the EMI for the same 20 years goes from ₹30,374 to ₹32,625. If you keep paying ₹30,374 instead, the loan takes about 309 months (25.8 years) to clear.

Is home loan interest tax-deductible in India?
It depends on your tax regime and the property. The Income Tax Department lists a deduction for interest on a housing loan under Section 24(b): for a self-occupied property under the old regime, up to ₹2,00,000 a year. Under the new regime its list shows the Section 24(b) deduction for let-out property only. Check the department&#x27;s page and your own situation before relying on it.

Does the EMI include insurance and processing fees?
No. The calculator shows interest and principal only. Processing fees, property or life insurance a lender bundles in, and other charges are separate.

Can I see the month-by-month schedule?
Yes. Open the full amortization schedule under the year-by-year table in the calculator.

### How a car loan EMI is worked out

A car loan EMI is a fixed monthly payment on a reducing-balance loan: EMI = [P x R x (1 + R)^N] / [(1 + R)^N - 1]. P is the amount you borrow, R is the monthly rate (annual rate / 12 / 100) and N is the number of months.
Worked example: ₹8,00,000 at 9.5 % for 5 years ( 60 months). The EMI is ₹16,801 a month. You pay ₹10,08,089 in total, of which ₹2,08,089 is interest, or 26% of the amount borrowed.

### The loan amount is the price minus your down payment

### Costs outside the EMI

The EMI covers principal and interest. A processing fee is extra: an example fee of 1 % on ₹8,00,000 is ₹8,000, which adds to what the loan costs you even though it is not in the EMI. Insurance and registration are also separate. Add them to your own budget when you compare offers.

### What this leaves out

This is the EMI maths only. It does not include the processing fee, insurance the dealer may offer to finance, registration charges, or a rate that changes during the loan. Your offer letter has the exact figures. To check whether an EMI fits your income, see the loan eligibility calculator; for a larger or longer loan, the home loan EMI calculator.

### Frequently asked questions

How is a car loan EMI calculated?
The same reducing-balance formula as any EMI: EMI = [P x R x (1 + R)^N] / [(1 + R)^N - 1]. For ₹8,00,000 at 9.5% for 5 years, the EMI is ₹16,801 and the total interest is ₹2,08,089.

What is the EMI for a 5 lakh car loan?
At 9.5% for 5 years, ₹5,00,000 gives an EMI of ₹10,501. For 3 years it is ₹16,016. The rate is an example; use the rate in your offer.

Should I include the down payment in the loan amount?
No. Enter only the amount you borrow, after subtracting your down payment from the vehicle&#x27;s on-road price. On a ₹10,00,000 car, a 20% down payment means borrowing ₹8,00,000.

Is a longer car loan tenure a good idea?
It lowers the EMI but raises the total interest. On ₹8,00,000 at 9.5%, 3 years costs ₹1,22,549 in interest and 7 years costs ₹2,98,316. Lenders set their own maximum tenure for car loans, so check the terms in your offer.

How much extra does a processing fee add?
It is on top of the EMI. An example fee of 1% on ₹8,00,000 is ₹8,000. Your offer states the actual fee and whether it is charged upfront or added to the loan.

How much does a one percentage point lower rate save?
On ₹8,00,000 over 5 years, 9.5% costs ₹2,08,089 in interest and 8.5% costs ₹1,84,794, a saving of ₹23,296.

Can I use this for a two-wheeler loan?
Yes. Enter the amount, rate and term. For example, ₹1,00,000 at 9.5% over 24 months is an EMI of ₹4,591. Set the term in years, so 24 months is 2.

Does my credit score affect the rate I am offered?
Lenders consider your credit history along with income, the loan size and their own policy, so the rate in your offer can differ from the rate you enter here. Always enter the rate from the offer you have.

Does the EMI cover insurance and registration?
No. The calculator shows principal and interest only. Insurance, registration and other charges are separate, whether you pay them upfront or finance them.

Year 10 ₹6,00,000 ₹11,61,695
The return rate is an assumption you set, not a guarantee. Mutual fund returns are market-linked and will differ from this projection.

### How a SIP projection is calculated

Future value = P x [((1 + i)^n - 1) / i] x (1 + i)

- P is the amount invested each month.
- i is the assumed monthly return: the annual return divided by 12, then by 100.
- n is the number of months invested.
It adds up a series of equal monthly investments, each growing at the assumed rate from the start of its month until the end. The first instalment grows for all n months and the last for one.

### How to use the SIP calculator

- Enter the monthly amount you could invest every month.
- Enter a return you assume. It is your assumption; no one can promise a return on a market-linked fund.
- Enter the years. The table shows the amount invested and the projected value at the end of each year.
Worked example: ₹5,000 a month for 10 years at an assumed 12 % a year. You invest ₹6,00,000 ( ₹5,000 x 120 months). The projected value is ₹11,61,695, so ₹5,61,695 of it is projected growth, if the 12 % held for the whole period.

### Projected value for different returns and durations

₹5,000 a month. The returns across the top are assumptions to compare, not predictions of what any fund will do.

### SIP compared with a lump sum

Suppose you invest the same total, ₹6,00,000, either as ₹5,000 a month for 10 years or as one lump sum on day one, at an assumed 12 % a year in both cases. The SIP projects to ₹11,61,695. The lump sum, compounded monthly, projects to ₹19,80,232. The lump sum is larger only because all of the money starts working on day one; most people do not have it on day one. A SIP fits the way income arrives. The compound interest calculator handles the lump sum.

### What this leaves out

This is a projection from one assumed, constant return rate. Real market returns vary from year to year and can be negative, so the actual result will differ. It does not include fund expenses, exit loads, taxes on gains, or any rise in your monthly amount over time. Read the fund&#x27;s documents before you invest.

### Frequently asked questions

What is a SIP?
A Systematic Investment Plan is a fixed amount invested into a mutual fund at a set interval, usually monthly, instead of one lump sum. You buy in at many different prices over time rather than at one price.

How is SIP future value calculated?
FV = P x [((1 + i)^n - 1) / i] x (1 + i), where P is the monthly amount, i is the assumed monthly return (annual return divided by 12 and by 100), and n is the number of months. The extra (1 + i) factor treats each instalment as invested at the start of its month.

How much will a SIP of 5,000 a month be worth in 10 years?
It depends on the return you assume, which nobody can promise. At an assumed 12% a year, ₹5,000 a month for 10 years invests ₹6,00,000 and projects to ₹11,61,695. At an assumed 8% it projects to ₹9,20,828, and at 6% to ₹8,23,494.

Is the return rate guaranteed?
No. The rate you enter is an assumption for projection only. Mutual fund SIPs are market-linked, and the actual return can be higher or lower than any rate you assume here, including negative in a bad year.

What return rate should I assume?
That is your own assumption to make, and the calculator does not suggest one. Try a low, a middle and a high figure, as the table on this page does, and plan around the low one.

Does starting early matter?
Yes, because time does more of the work than the amount. At an assumed 12%, ₹5,000 a month for 30 years projects to ₹1,76,49,569, while 20 years projects to ₹49,95,740. The table on this page shows the cost of waiting.

Is SIP better than a lump sum investment?
Neither is better in every case. With the same return assumed, a lump sum invested on day one grows more than a SIP of the same total, because more money is invested earlier: ₹19,80,232 against ₹11,61,695 for ₹6,00,000 over 10 years at 12%. A SIP fits money that arrives monthly, and it avoids choosing one day to invest everything.

What is the difference between a SIP and a recurring deposit?
A recurring deposit pays a rate fixed by the bank. A mutual fund SIP buys fund units, whose value moves with the market, so there is no fixed rate. For a fixed-rate deposit, use the compound interest calculator.

Does this include taxes, fees and fund charges?
No. It shows the gross projection at the rate you enter. Fund expenses, exit loads and taxes on gains reduce what you keep, so read the fund&#x27;s documents and a current tax guide.

# Loan Eligibility Calculator: Max Loan from Income

## Loan Eligibility Calculator

Enter your monthly income, any existing EMIs, and a loan rate and tenure to see roughly how large a loan your income could support, using the FOIR approach lenders commonly apply.
Net monthly income (₹)
Existing EMIs per month (₹)
Lender&#x27;s EMI limit, FOIR (%) Each lender sets its own limit; 50% is the default here
Interest rate, per year (%)
Loan term (years)

Loan amount you likely qualify for ₹14,45,201
Affordable EMI ₹30,000
Total interest on that loan ₹3,54,799

An estimate based on income and existing EMIs only. Lenders also weigh credit score, employment type, age, collateral and their own policy, so the real sanctioned amount can differ.

### How loan eligibility is estimated

Lenders commonly size a loan by capping all monthly EMIs, the new one plus existing ones, at a share of net income. That share is the Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR). Each lender sets its own, so the figure is yours to change here. The estimate works in three steps:

- Take the FOIR share of your income. 50 % of ₹60,000 is ₹30,000, your total EMI budget.
- Subtract your existing EMIs. With none, the whole ₹30,000 is available for the new loan.
- Run that EMI through the formula in reverse. Loan = EMI x [(1 + R)^N - 1] / [R x (1 + R)^N], with R the monthly rate and N the months. At 9 % for 5 years this gives ₹14,45,201.
Check: the EMI on ₹14,45,201 at 9 % for 5 years is ₹30,000. For any loan amount, the EMI calculator shows the EMI directly.

### Loan amount by income and tenure

With a 50 % limit, no existing EMIs and an example rate of 9 %. The rate is an assumption for the table; use the rate you are offered in the calculator.
Net monthly income EMI budget Loan over 5 years Loan over 10 years Loan over 20 years
₹30,000 ₹15,000 ₹7,22,601 ₹11,84,125 ₹16,67,174
₹50,000 ₹25,000 ₹12,04,334 ₹19,73,542 ₹27,78,624
₹75,000 ₹37,500 ₹18,06,502 ₹29,60,313 ₹41,67,936
₹1,00,000 ₹50,000 ₹24,08,669 ₹39,47,085 ₹55,57,248
₹1,50,000 ₹75,000 ₹36,13,003 ₹59,20,627 ₹83,35,872

### What this leaves out

Real approval also depends on your credit history, how stable your employment is, your age when the loan would end, the value of the asset for a secured loan, and the lender&#x27;s own risk policy. Treat the figure here as a starting estimate to plan around, not a sanction amount. It also does not include fees or insurance. For the full cost of a loan you are considering, use the home loan EMI or car loan EMI calculator.

### Frequently asked questions

What is FOIR, and why does it matter for loan eligibility?
FOIR, Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio, is the share of your net monthly income that goes to all EMIs combined, including the new loan. Each lender sets its own limit. This calculator uses 50% as a default and lets you change it. At 50% on ₹60,000 a month, your total EMI budget is ₹30,000.

How is loan eligibility calculated?
Your EMI budget is net income x FOIR minus existing EMIs. That EMI is then run through the EMI formula in reverse, at your rate and term, to get the loan amount. ₹30,000 a month at 9% for 5 years supports about ₹14,45,201.

How does an existing EMI affect how much I can borrow?
It is subtracted from your EMI budget before the new loan is sized. At a 50% limit on ₹1,00,000 of income, the budget is ₹50,000; a ₹10,000 existing EMI leaves ₹40,000, and at 9% for 20 years that supports about ₹44,45,798 instead of ₹55,57,248.

Does a longer tenure increase how much I can borrow?
Yes. The same EMI supports a larger principal over a longer term. ₹30,000 a month at 9% supports about ₹14,45,201 over 5 years and ₹33,34,349 over 20 years. A longer term also means more total interest, so compare it on the EMI calculator.

Should I use gross or net income?
Net monthly income: what reaches your account after tax and other deductions. Using gross income overstates what you can set aside for EMIs.

Why might a bank approve less than this calculator shows?
This estimate only looks at income, existing EMIs, rate and term. Lenders also look at your credit history, employment, age, the value of what you are buying and their own policy, any of which can change the amount offered.

Can I include a co-applicant&#x27;s income?
Add the net incomes together and enter the total, and add the EMIs of both applicants to existing EMIs. How a lender treats a joint application is up to the lender.

How can I improve my eligibility?
Clear or reduce existing EMIs, add a co-applicant&#x27;s income, choose a longer term, or look for a lower rate. Each one raises the EMI budget or the loan it supports. A longer term raises total interest.

Is a loan I qualify for a loan I can afford?
Not necessarily. A high FOIR leaves less of your income for everything else. Use the EMI calculator to check the EMI against your own monthly costs before you take the full amount.

# GST Calculator India: Add or Remove GST (5%, 18%, 40%)

URL: https://calc.streamerosai.com/gst-calculator/

Free · instant · no sign-up

## GST Calculator

Add GST to a price, or pull it back out of a price that already includes tax, at 5%, 18%, 40% or any rate you enter, with the CGST and SGST split shown.

Amount before GST (₹)
GST rate (%) 5 % 18 % 40 % 12 % (rate before 22 Sep 2025) 28 % (rate before 22 Sep 2025) Other rate

Total, including GST ₹1,180.00
GST amount ₹180.00
CGST + SGST ₹90.00 + ₹90.00

CGST and SGST (split evenly) apply within one state; an inter-state sale charges the same total as IGST instead.

### How GST is added and removed

Adding GST (price without tax known): GST amount = base x rate / 100; total = base + GST amount.
Removing GST (price with tax known): base = total / (1 + rate / 100); GST amount = total - base. This is the direction people get wrong most often: the rate was added to the base, so you divide the total by (1 + rate / 100). Taking the rate off the total overstates the GST.

### Worked examples

- Add 18% to ₹1,000. GST is ₹180. Total is ₹1,180. For a sale within one state, that is ₹90 CGST and ₹90 SGST.
- Remove 18% from ₹1,180. Base = ₹1,180 / 1.18 = ₹1,000. GST = ₹1,180 - ₹1,000 = ₹180.
- The common mistake. ₹1,180 x 18% = ₹212.40, which would leave a base of ₹967.60. That is not the original ₹1,000.

### GST rates in India

The GST Council&#x27;s 56th meeting (3 September 2025) recommended replacing the four-tier rate structure with two main rates: a standard rate of 18% and a merit rate of 5%, plus a special rate of 40% for a select few goods and services. The changes on services, and on goods other than a few tobacco products, took effect on 22 September 2025. The 12% and 28% slabs that applied before are no longer used for new supplies of most items, but they still appear on invoices dated before the change. The rate for a particular item is set in the rate notification, so look the item up there; this page does not list items.
GST rate GST on ₹1,000 Total with GST CGST + SGST (within a state) GST inside ₹1,000
5 % ₹50.00 ₹1,050.00 ₹25.00 + ₹25.00 ₹47.62
12 % (before 22 Sep 2025) ₹120.00 ₹1,120.00 ₹60.00 + ₹60.00 ₹107.14
18 % ₹180.00 ₹1,180.00 ₹90.00 + ₹90.00 ₹152.54
28 % (before 22 Sep 2025) ₹280.00 ₹1,280.00 ₹140.00 + ₹140.00 ₹218.75
40 % ₹400.00 ₹1,400.00 ₹200.00 + ₹200.00 ₹285.71
The last column answers the other question: if ₹1,000 is the price including GST, this is the tax inside it.

### Which rate applies when a rate changes

When a rate changes, the rate follows the time of supply. The GST Council&#x27;s FAQs on the 2025 changes work through cases such as goods supplied before the change but invoiced after it, and advances received before it. They refer to Section 14 of the CGST Act. If you have such an invoice, read those FAQs or ask a tax professional; the calculator only does the arithmetic once you choose the rate.

### CGST, SGST and IGST

For a supply within one state, the GST is shown as CGST (central) and SGST (state), each half of the rate: at 18% that is 9% and 9%. For a supply between states, the same total is charged once as IGST. The GST amount is the same either way, which is why this calculator shows one GST figure and the even split beside it.

### What this calculator leaves out

It does the arithmetic on one price at one rate. It does not know which rate applies to your item, it does not include input tax credit, cess or reverse charge, and it does not rework invoices that mix rates. For a percentage of any amount, use the percentage calculator; for income tax, the India income tax calculator.

### Sources

- GST Council: recommendations of the 56th meeting (press release, 3 September 2025) (the 5%, 18% and 40% structure and the 22 September 2025 date), checked 16 November 2026.
- GST Council: FAQs on the decisions of the 56th meeting (time of supply when rates change), checked 16 November 2026.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I add GST to a price?
GST amount = price x (rate / 100); total = price + GST amount. For ₹1,000 at 18%, GST is ₹180 and the total is ₹1,180.

How do I remove GST from a price that already includes it?
Base price = total / (1 + rate / 100); GST amount = total - base price. For a ₹1,180 total at 18%, the base price is ₹1,000 and the GST portion is ₹180.

What are the GST rates in India now?
After the 56th GST Council meeting, most goods and services moved to a two-rate structure: a standard rate of 18% and a merit rate of 5%, with a special rate of 40% for a few goods and services. The changes took effect on 22 September 2025, except for cigarettes, chewing tobacco products and similar goods, which kept their existing rates until a later date to be notified.

Are the 12% and 28% GST rates still used?
Not for new supplies of most goods and services: the Council&#x27;s changes replaced them with 5% and 18% (or 40% for some goods and services). They still appear on invoices for supplies made before 22 September 2025, so this calculator lists them as older rates. Which rate applies to a specific item is in the rate notification.

Which GST rate applies if the invoice date and the supply date are on different sides of a rate change?
The rate follows the time of supply rules in Section 14 of the CGST Act. The GST Council&#x27;s FAQs explain how it works when goods or services were supplied before a change and invoiced after, and for advances. Read the FAQ linked in the sources, or ask a tax professional about your case.

What is the difference between CGST, SGST and IGST?
For a sale within one state, GST is shown as CGST (central) and SGST (state), each half of the total rate. For a sale between states, the full rate is charged once as IGST. Either way, the total tax is the same, which is why the GST amount in this calculator does not change.

How do I calculate 18% GST on 1,000?
₹1,000 x 18% = ₹180 of GST, so the total is ₹1,180. Split evenly, that is ₹90 CGST and ₹90 SGST within one state.

Why can&#x27;t I just take 18% off a GST-inclusive price?
Because the 18% was added to the base price, not to the total. Taking 18% off ₹1,180 gives ₹967.60, which is wrong. The correct base is ₹1,000.00.

Can I use a rate that is not in the list?
Yes. Choose Other rate and type any percentage, for example a rate shown on an older invoice or a special rate for a particular item.

# Compound Interest Calculator: Maturity Value by Year

#### Year-by-year growth

Year Value Interest that year
Year 1 ₹1,08,000 ₹8,000
Year 2 ₹1,16,640 ₹8,640
Year 3 ₹1,25,971 ₹9,331
Year 4 ₹1,36,049 ₹10,078
Year 5 ₹1,46,933 ₹10,884
Year 6 ₹1,58,687 ₹11,755

Year 8 ₹1,85,093 ₹13,711
Year 9 ₹1,99,900 ₹14,807
Year 10 ₹2,15,892 ₹15,992

### The compound interest formula

A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt)

- P is the principal amount invested.
- r is the annual interest rate as a decimal (8% is 0.08).
- n is how many times a year interest compounds (1 annually, 4 quarterly, 12 monthly).
- t is the time in years.
Compounding means interest is added to the balance and then earns interest itself. The interest earned is A minus P.

### How to calculate compound interest

- Divide the rate by the periods. 8 % compounded annually: 0.08 / 1 = 0.08. Monthly: 0.08 / 12 = 0.006667.
- Count the periods. 10 years x 1 = 10 periods, or 10 x 12 = 120 for monthly.
- Raise (1 + r/n) to the number of periods and multiply by the principal.
Worked example: ₹1,00,000 at 8 % for 10 years, compounded annually, grows to ₹2,15,892. That is ₹1,15,892 of interest. Compounded monthly, the same 8 % grows it to ₹2,21,964.

### Compounding frequency compared

₹1,00,000 at 8 % for 10 years, changing only how often interest is added. The effective annual rate is the yearly rate that would give the same result.
Compounded Maturity value Interest Effective annual rate
Annually ₹2,15,892 ₹1,15,892 8%
Semi-annually ₹2,19,112 ₹1,19,112 8.16%
Quarterly ₹2,20,804 ₹1,20,804 8.243%
Monthly ₹2,21,964 ₹1,21,964 8.3%
Daily (365) ₹2,22,535 ₹1,22,535 8.328%

### Growth of ₹1,00,000 at different rates and times

Compounded annually. The rates are examples to compare, not rates any product pays.
Rate After 5 years After 10 years After 20 years After 30 years
4 % ₹1,21,665 ₹1,48,024 ₹2,19,112 ₹3,24,340
6 % ₹1,33,823 ₹1,79,085 ₹3,20,714 ₹5,74,349
8 % ₹1,46,933 ₹2,15,892 ₹4,66,096 ₹10,06,266
10 % ₹1,61,051 ₹2,59,374 ₹6,72,750 ₹17,44,940
12 % ₹1,76,234 ₹3,10,585 ₹9,64,629 ₹29,95,992

### Simple interest compared

Simple interest is P x r x t, with no interest on interest. On ₹1,00,000 at 8 % for 10 years it is ₹1,00,000 x 0.08 x 10 = ₹80,000, so the total is ₹1,80,000. Compound interest gives ₹2,15,892, which is ₹35,892 more. The gap widens every year, because the compounding balance keeps growing.

### How long to double your money

The rule of 72 is a shortcut: years to double are about 72 divided by the rate. The exact figure for annual compounding is ln 2 / ln(1 + r).
Rate Rule of 72 Exact (annual compounding)
4 % 18.0 years 17.7 years
6 % 12.0 years 11.9 years
8 % 9.0 years 9.0 years
10 % 7.2 years 7.3 years
12 % 6.0 years 6.1 years

### What this leaves out

It assumes one fixed rate and no deposits or withdrawals, and it does not include tax on the interest or any fees. Real products can use day counts or rounding rules that change the last few rupees. To model regular monthly investing, use the SIP calculator, and for loan repayments the EMI calculator.

### Frequently asked questions

What is the compound interest formula?
A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), where P is the principal, r is the annual rate as a decimal, n is the number of compounding periods per year, and t is the time in years. The total interest earned is A minus P.

How do I calculate compound interest on 1 lakh for 10 years?
At an example rate of 8% compounded annually, ₹1,00,000 grows to ₹2,15,892 in 10 years, which is ₹1,15,892 of interest. Compounded monthly it grows to ₹2,21,964.

What is the difference between compound and simple interest?
Simple interest is worked out on the original principal only, so it adds the same amount each year. Compound interest is worked out on the principal plus the interest already earned. On ₹1,00,000 at 8% for 10 years, simple interest gives ₹1,80,000 and annual compounding gives ₹2,15,892.

Does compounding frequency make a big difference?
It makes some difference, but less than the rate or the time. At 8% for 10 years on ₹1,00,000, annual compounding gives ₹2,15,892 and monthly gives ₹2,21,964, a gap of ₹6,072. Raising the rate by two points to 10% changes the annual result by far more.

What is the effective annual rate?
The yearly rate that gives the same result as the stated rate compounded more often. 8% compounded monthly has an effective annual rate of 8.3%. The calculator shows it as a tile.

How long does it take to double my money?
At 8% compounded annually, a little over 9.0 years. The rule of 72 estimates it as 72 divided by the rate: 72 / 8 = 9 years.

How do I find the time needed to reach a target?
Rearrange the formula: t = ln(A / P) / (n x ln(1 + r/n)). To grow ₹1,00,000 to ₹2,00,000 at 8% compounded annually, t = ln(2) / ln(1.08) = 9.01 years.

Which products pay compound interest?
A deposit or bond that adds its interest to the balance and then earns interest on it compounds, at the frequency its terms state. A mutual fund does not pay a fixed rate; for market-linked, assumed returns on monthly investments, use the SIP calculator.

Why does my bank&#x27;s figure differ slightly from this calculator?
A bank can use the actual number of days in a period or round at each compounding date, which gives small differences from the textbook formula used here. Your deposit receipt or account terms have the exact method.
