# Income Tax Calculator India: New vs Old Regime (FY 2026-27)

URL: https://calc.streamerosai.com/income-tax-calculator-india/

Free · instant · no sign-up

## Income Tax Calculator (India)

Enter your annual income to see your India income tax for FY 2026-27 (AY 2027-28) under the new or old regime, with every step of the working shown.

Annual income (₹)
Income type Salaried (gets the standard deduction) Other income (no standard deduction)

Total tax payable ₹0
Take-home income ₹12,00,000
Effective tax rate 0.0 %

Working Amount
Gross income ₹12,00,000
Standard deduction - ₹75,000
Taxable income ₹11,25,000
Tax before rebate ₹52,500
Section 87A rebate - ₹52,500
Health and education cess (4%) ₹0
Total tax ₹0

### How the calculator works it out

The calculator follows the same order as the tax law, and the working table under the result shows each line, so you can check it against your own payslip or Form 16.

- Start from gross income for the year: salary before any deduction, or other income.
- Subtract the standard deduction if the income is salary: ₹75,000 in the new regime, ₹50,000 in the old one.
- Old regime only, subtract Section 80C and 80D, each capped: up to ₹1,50,000 for 80C investments and up to ₹25,000 for 80D health insurance. What is left is taxable income.
- Apply the slab rates in the tables below, each rate only to the part of taxable income that falls inside its band.
- Take off the Section 87A rebate if taxable income is at or under the threshold (₹12 lakh new, ₹5 lakh old).
- Add 4 % health and education cess on the tax that remains. That total is your tax for the year; gross income minus it is the take-home figure.

### New regime slabs, FY 2026-27 (AY 2027-28)

Taxable income Rate
Up to ₹4,00,000 Nil
₹4,00,000 to ₹8,00,000 5%
₹8,00,000 to ₹12,00,000 10%
₹12,00,000 to ₹16,00,000 15%
₹16,00,000 to ₹20,00,000 20%
₹20,00,000 to ₹24,00,000 25%
Above ₹24,00,000 30%
Rates apply only to the slice of income inside each range, not the whole amount. A ₹75,000 standard deduction applies first for salaried income, then the Section 87A rebate cancels the tax entirely if taxable income is ₹12,00,000 or under. A 4 % health and education cess applies on top of whatever tax remains.

### Old regime slabs

Taxable income Rate
Up to ₹2,50,000 (₹3,00,000 if 60-79, ₹5,00,000 if 80+) Nil
Next slab up to ₹5,00,000 5%
₹5,00,000 to ₹10,00,000 20%
Above ₹10,00,000 30%
The old regime allows Sections 80C and 80D (modelled here) plus others this calculator doesn&#x27;t cover, such as HRA and home loan interest, and its standard deduction is ₹50,000 for salaried income. Its Section 87A rebate cancels tax only up to ₹5,00,000 taxable income.

### Worked example: a ₹15 lakh salary in both regimes

A salaried employee under 60 earns ₹15,00,000 a year. In the old regime they also invest the full ₹1,50,000 under Section 80C and pay ₹25,000 of health insurance premium.
Working New regime Old regime
Gross income ₹15,00,000 ₹15,00,000
Standard deduction - ₹75,000 - ₹50,000
Section 80C + 80D not allowed - ₹1,75,000
Taxable income ₹14,25,000 ₹12,75,000
Tax on the slabs ₹93,750 ₹1,95,000
Section 87A rebate ₹0 (over ₹12 lakh) ₹0 (over ₹5 lakh)
Cess at 4 % ₹3,750 ₹7,800
Total tax ₹97,500 ₹2,02,800
Effective rate on gross income 6.5 % 13.5 %
The new-regime slab tax is built up band by band: nothing on the first ₹4,00,000, ₹20,000 on the next ₹4,00,000 at 5%, ₹40,000 on the next ₹4,00,000 at 10%, and ₹33,750 on the last ₹2,25,000 at 15%, which makes ₹93,750. In the old regime the same person pays ₹12,500 on ₹2,50,000 to ₹5,00,000 at 5%, ₹1,00,000 on ₹5,00,000 to ₹10,00,000 at 20%, and ₹82,500 on the last ₹2,75,000 at 30%. Even with both deductions used in full, the new regime costs ₹1,05,300 less a year here.

### How much in deductions the old regime needs

At a ₹15,00,000 salary the old regime only catches up when its taxable income falls to ₹9,06,250, where its slab tax equals the new regime&#x27;s ₹93,750. That takes ₹5,43,750 of deductions on top of the ₹50,000 standard deduction. Sections 80C and 80D together allow at most ₹1,75,000, so the rest would have to come from deductions this calculator does not model, mainly HRA and home loan interest. If you do not have those, the new regime is almost certainly cheaper at this income. If you do, add them up before you choose, because the answer turns on that total rather than on your salary alone.

### Just above the ₹12 lakh line

A salary of ₹13,00,000 in the new regime leaves ₹12,25,000 of taxable income after the standard deduction. That is above ₹12,00,000, so the 87A rebate no longer applies and the calculator shows the full slab tax of ₹63,750 plus ₹2,550 cess, ₹66,300 in all. The law softens this cliff with marginal relief, which this calculator does not apply, so for taxable income a little over ₹12 lakh your actual tax will be lower than the figure shown. Treat the result in this band as an upper limit and check it with the Income Tax Department&#x27;s calculator.

### When to use it

- Choosing a regime at the start of the year. Salaried employees tell their employer which regime to use for tax deducted from salary; run your income through both tabs first.
- Weighing a raise or a job offer. Enter the new gross figure to see how much of the increase you keep, and whether it crosses the ₹12 lakh rebate line.
- Deciding whether an 80C investment is worth it for tax. In the old regime, compare the result with 80C at zero and at ₹1,50,000; in the new regime it makes no difference.

### What this estimate leaves out

This is a slab-and-rebate estimate, not a filing. It does not include surcharge on incomes above ₹50 lakh, the exact marginal relief just above either rebate threshold, special rates on capital gains or similar income, or old-regime deductions beyond Sections 80C and 80D such as HRA, home loan interest or NPS. Use it to plan, and a CA or the Income Tax Department&#x27;s own calculator for a return you&#x27;re filing.
Two simplifications in the inputs: Section 80D is capped at ₹25,000, the limit for a policy covering yourself and your family when you are under 60, so the higher limits for senior citizens and for a separate policy for your parents are not included. And the age choice only appears in the old regime, because the new regime&#x27;s slabs are the same at every age.

### Sources

- PIB, Union Budget 2025-26: “No Income Tax On Annual Income Upto Rs. 12 Lakh Under New Tax Regime” (new regime slabs, ₹75,000 standard deduction, ₹12 lakh / ₹12.75 lakh tax-free limit), 1 Feb 2025.
- ClearTax: Income Tax Slabs FY 2025-26 & FY 2026-27 (confirms Budget 2026-27 made no change for FY 2026-27, and the old regime figures), checked 11 Nov 2026.
- Income Tax Department: Tax Rates (one rate table listed for AY 2025-26 and AY 2026-27), checked 11 Nov 2026.
- Finance Bill 2026 memorandum (4% health and education cess), 2 Feb 2026.

### Frequently asked questions

Is income up to ₹12 lakh really tax-free in the new regime?
Yes, for FY 2026-27. The slab rates on taxable income up to ₹12,00,000 add up to ₹60,000 of tax, and the Section 87A rebate cancels exactly that amount, so the net tax is zero. For a salaried taxpayer, the ₹75,000 standard deduction pushes the effective tax-free gross income up to ₹12,75,000.

Did Budget 2026 change the income tax slabs?
No. Union Budget 2026-27 (presented 1 February 2026) made no change to the income tax slabs, standard deduction or Section 87A rebate for either regime, so the FY 2025-26 figures carry over unchanged to FY 2026-27.

Which regime should I choose?
The new regime is the default and usually works out better if you claim few deductions. The old regime can work out better if your Section 80C, 80D and other deductions (including HRA and home loan interest, not modelled in this calculator) are large relative to your income. Run both and compare.

What is the Section 87A rebate?
A rebate that cancels tax up to a cap, provided taxable income is under a threshold: up to ₹60,000 for taxable income up to ₹12,00,000 in the new regime, or up to ₹12,500 for taxable income up to ₹5,00,000 in the old regime. Just above either threshold, marginal relief (not modelled here) limits how fast the tax reappears.

Is the standard deduction the same in both regimes?
No. It&#x27;s ₹75,000 in the new regime and ₹50,000 in the old regime, and either way it only applies to salaried income, not business or other income.

# Currency Converter: Convert Any Currency at Live Rates

## Currency Converter

Convert between any two currencies at live exchange rates. Pick the currencies, enter an amount, and see the result, the rate and a table of common amounts.
Amount
From USD INR EUR GBP AUD CAD AED SGD JPY CHF
To USD INR EUR GBP AUD CAD AED SGD JPY CHF

Loading live rates...

### How to use the converter

- Enter the amount you want to convert.
- Choose the currency you have in From and the one you want in To.
- Read the converted amount and the rate. Use Swap currencies to reverse the direction.

### How a currency conversion is calculated

Converted amount = amount x exchange rate. The rate says how much of the second currency one unit of the first buys. The reverse rate is one divided by it.
Rates are quoted against one reference currency. To convert from currency A to currency B, the amount is divided by A&#x27;s rate and multiplied by B&#x27;s rate, which gives the same answer as the direct A to B rate. Worked example, with made-up rates for the arithmetic only: if 1 US dollar is 0.8 euros and 90 rupees, then 5,000 euros is 5000 / 0.8 = 6,250 dollars, and that is 6,250 x 90 = ₹5,62,500. The direct euro to rupee rate is 90 / 0.8 = 112.5.

### Popular pairs

These pages open the converter with the pair already selected, with notes specific to each currency:

- USD to INR
- INR to USD
- GBP to INR
- EUR to INR
- CAD to INR
- AUD to INR
- AED to INR
For a salary or hourly wage in another currency, use the USD salary to INR calculator, which also splits the result by month, week and hour.

### What a margin costs you

The rate shown here is the mid-market rate. A bank, card or transfer app usually gives you a rate below it, a margin, and may add a fixed fee on top. This table shows what different margins take from a 1,000 unit transfer at an example rate of 90. The margins are examples, not what any provider charges.
Margin below mid-market Rate you get You receive Lost to the margin
None (mid-market) 90.00 90,000 0
0.5 % 89.55 89,550 450
1 % 89.10 89,100 900
2 % 88.20 88,200 1,800
3 % 87.30 87,300 2,700
5 % 85.50 85,500 4,500
Compare the final amount that arrives, not the headline rate. Why your bank&#x27;s number differs, and what a good deal looks like, is covered in how exchange rates work.

### What this converter leaves out

It shows the mid-market reference rate, not a rate you can trade at. It does not include provider margins, fixed fees, or taxes on a transfer. The rate comes from a free feed updated about once a day, so it can be a few hours behind the market. Use it to plan and check, and confirm the final figure with your provider.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I convert one currency to another?
Multiply the amount by the exchange rate from the first currency to the second. If 1 euro buys 1.25 US dollars (an example rate), then 50 euros is 50 x 1.25 = 62.5 dollars. The converter does this with live rates.

How do I convert between two currencies that are not the dollar?
Rates are quoted against one reference currency, so the converter goes through it. With example rates of 1 USD = 0.8 EUR and 1 USD = 90 INR, 5,000 EUR is 5000 / 0.8 x 90 = ₹5,62,500. The direct EUR to INR rate is 90 / 0.8 = 112.5.

How do I find the reverse rate?
Divide 1 by the rate. If 1 US dollar is 90 rupees (an example), 1 rupee is 1 / 90 = 0.0111 dollars. The converter shows both directions under the result.

Which currencies can I convert?
Any two currencies in the lists, including US dollars, euros, pounds, rupees, Australian and Canadian dollars, dirhams, yen and many more. The pickers show the currencies your browser knows, with the popular ones first. A currency with no published rate shows a message instead of a result.

Where do the exchange rates come from?
From a free public rates feed that publishes mid-market reference rates about once a day, with two backup feeds. The date of the rates is shown under each result.

Is this the rate I will get at a bank or exchange counter?
No. This is the mid-market rate. Banks, card networks and transfer apps apply their own margin or fee, so the amount you receive is lower. Compare the final amount, not the headline rate.

How do I check whether a transfer is good value?
Divide the amount that arrives by the amount you sent to get the rate you really got, then compare it with the mid-market rate shown here. For example, if 1,000 dollars arrives as ₹88,650 when the example rate is 90, you got 88.65 rupees a dollar, which is 1.5% below the mid-market rate. Include any fixed fee in the amount.

Why does the rate change during the day?
Currencies trade continuously, so rates move. The feed this page uses publishes about once a day, so the rate shown can differ from a live market quote and from the rate a provider shows you.

What if the rates will not load?
If none of the feeds can be reached, the converter lets you type a rate yourself, so you can still do the sum.

### How to convert a dollar salary to rupees

The calculator converts your pay between periods first (hourly, weekly, monthly, annual) using your schedule, then converts each figure from dollars to rupees at the live rate. The left column is in the currency you chose and the right column is in the second currency.
Rupee pay = dollar pay x USD to INR rate.

- Get the dollar figure for one period. $60,000 a year, or $25 an hour.
- Multiply by the rate. At an example rate of 90, that is ₹54,00,000 a year.
- Split it into periods. That is ₹4,50,000.00 a month, ₹1,03,846.15 a week and ₹2,596.15 an hour at 2,080 hours a year.
The rates on this page are round example numbers to show the arithmetic. They are not today&#x27;s rate; the calculator above loads that.

### Before you compare

- Compare after tax. A US salary and an Indian salary of the same rupee value are taxed under different rules. See the paycheck calculator for US take-home pay and the India income tax calculator for Indian tax.
- Compare against your costs. The same rupee amount buys different things in different places, so an exchange-rate conversion alone does not tell you how well off you would be.
- Remember the transfer. If you are paid in dollars and spend in rupees, what you receive depends on the rate your bank or transfer service gives, which is below the mid-market rate shown here. See how exchange rates work.

### What this calculator leaves out

It converts gross pay at the mid-market rate. It does not include income tax in either country, benefits, bonuses, or the margin and fees on moving money between currencies. For other pairs and a plain amount, use the currency converter or the USD to INR converter.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I convert a USD salary to INR?
Multiply the dollar salary by the USD to INR exchange rate. At an example rate of 90, a $60,000 salary is 60,000 x 90 = ₹54,00,000 a year. The calculator uses the live rate and also splits the result by month, week and hour.

How much is a $100,000 salary in rupees?
It depends on the rate on the day. At example rates of 80, 90 and 100, it is ₹80,00,000, ₹90,00,000 and ₹1,00,00,000 a year. Enter the amount above for today&#x27;s figure.

How do I convert a dollar monthly salary to INR?
Multiply by the rate. At an example rate of 90, $5,000 a month is 5,000 x 90 = ₹4,50,000 a month, and ₹54,00,000 a year.

How do I convert an hourly wage in dollars to rupees?
Choose Hourly in the Per list and enter the dollar rate. You get the hourly figure in rupees plus the annual, monthly and weekly amounts, using your own hours per week. At an example rate of 90, $25 an hour is ₹2,250 an hour, or ₹46,80,000 a year at 2,080 hours.

Is the rupee figure what lands in my bank account?
No. It is the gross amount at the mid-market rate. Income tax, deductions, and the margin or fees of the bank or transfer service all reduce what you receive.

How much does a change in the rate matter?
On a $60,000 salary, every 1 rupee of change in the rate moves the yearly rupee amount by ₹60,000, which is ₹5,000 a month. A move from 90 to 91 is ₹60,000 a year.

Which rate does the calculator use?
The latest mid-market USD to INR rate from a free public feed, loaded when you open the page. The date is shown under the result.

Can I use another currency?
Yes. Change the currency and the Also show in list to any pair, for example a pound salary shown in rupees, or a rupee salary shown in dollars.

Is a dollar salary comparable with a rupee salary?
Only roughly. The conversion gives the same amount at the exchange rate, but taxes differ and prices differ between countries, so compare after tax and against your own costs.

### How to convert USD to INR

- Type the amount in USD. The currencies are already set to USD and INR.
- The result and the exchange rate update as soon as live rates load.
- Use Swap currencies to convert INR back to USD, or pick any other currency from the lists.

### About the USD to INR pair

The US dollar (USD) and the Indian rupee (INR) are among the most searched currency pairs in the world, mostly because of money moving between the two countries: family remittances, salaries paid in dollars, student fees and imports.
The rupee floats against the dollar, so the rate changes through the day and the figure you see here will differ slightly from a bank&#x27;s quote. Rupee amounts are shown in the Indian grouping, where 1,00,000 is one lakh and 1,00,00,000 is one crore.

### Common reasons to convert USD to INR

- Sending money to family in India, or receiving it.
- Converting a salary or freelance payment quoted in dollars. For that, use the USD salary to INR calculator, which also gives monthly and hourly pay.
- Estimating tuition, travel or shopping costs in dollars against a rupee budget.
- Checking an import or export price.

### USD to INR: the arithmetic

INR amount = USD amount x rate. To show the sum, this table uses a made-up round rate of 1 USD = 90 INR. It is not today&#x27;s rate; the converter above loads that.
USD INR at the example rate
$1.00 ₹90.00
$10.00 ₹900.00
$100.00 ₹9,000.00
$1,000.00 ₹90,000.00
$10,000.00 ₹9,00,000.00
To go back, divide by the rate: ₹9,000.00 is $100.00 at the same example rate. The reverse rate is 1 / 90 = 0.011111 USD per INR.

### What converting there and back costs

A provider that takes a margin of 2 % below the mid-market rate each way (an example, not any provider&#x27;s rate) leaves you with less than you started with. Start with $1,000.00: after the first leg you hold the equivalent of $980.00, and after converting back $960.40, a loss of $39.60. Convert once, in the direction you need.

### Why the rate you get is not the rate shown

The rate above is the mid-market rate. Banks, cards and transfer apps usually add a margin or a fee, so always compare the final amount that arrives. How exchange rates work explains the difference.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I convert USD to INR?
Multiply the dollar amount by the USD to INR rate. If 1 dollar buys 90 rupees, then 100 dollars is 100 x 90 = 9,000 rupees. The converter above does this with the latest rate.

What is 1 dollar in rupees today?
The tile above shows today&#x27;s rate, loaded live. 1 dollar to rupees is simply the rate itself.

Why is the rate different from my bank or money transfer app?
This page shows the mid-market rate, the midpoint between buying and selling prices. Banks and transfer services give you a less favourable rate or add a fee, so compare the amount that actually arrives.

Is the dollar to rupee rate fixed?
No. The rupee&#x27;s value against the dollar changes continuously with the foreign exchange market.

What is a lakh and a crore?
A lakh is 100,000 and a crore is 10,000,000. They are written 1,00,000 and 1,00,00,000 in Indian grouping, which is how rupee amounts appear above.

### Frequently asked questions

How do I convert rupees to dollars?
Divide the rupee amount by the USD to INR rate, or multiply it by the INR to USD rate. If 1 dollar is 90 rupees, then 9,000 rupees is 9,000 / 90 = 100 dollars. The converter does this with the live rate.

How many dollars is one lakh rupees?
One lakh is 100,000 rupees. Enter 100000 above to see the dollar amount at today&#x27;s rate. It changes through the day because the rupee floats against the dollar.

What is the difference between INR to USD and USD to INR?
They are the same exchange rate read in opposite directions. If 1 dollar buys 90 rupees, 1 rupee buys 1 / 90, about 0.0111 dollars. Use the swap button to flip the pair.

Why does my bank give me fewer dollars?
The page shows the mid-market rate. Banks and transfer services use a rate with their margin built in, and may add a fee, so the dollars you receive are lower. Compare the final amount, not the headline rate.

Is the rate updated live?
It is loaded from a public rates feed when you open the page. These feeds publish about once a day, and the date of the rates is shown under the result.

### Related tools

Currency Converter USD to INR: US Dollar to Indian Rupee GBP to INR: British Pound to Indian Rupee EUR to INR: Euro to Indian Rupee

Last reviewed 2026-11-16.

# How to Convert Salary to Hourly Pay (the 2,080-Hour Rule)

URL: https://calc.streamerosai.com/guides/salary-to-hourly/

## How to convert salary to hourly pay (the 2,080-hour rule)

To compare a salaried job with an hourly one, or to see what your time is worth, convert one into the other. The method is short, and the one number that matters is how many hours the year contains.

### The formula

hourly pay = annual salary / (hours per week x weeks per year) For a standard full-time job that is 40 hours x 52 weeks = 2,080 hours. So a $60,000 salary is $60,000 / 2,080 = $28.85 an hour. Going the other way, $28.85 x 2,080 comes back to about $60,000.

### Where 2,080 comes from

It is nothing more than 40 x 52. It treats every week of the year as a paid, 40-hour week, which includes paid vacation, paid holidays and sick days, because a salary pays for those weeks too. That is why the same number works for people who do not literally clock 2,080 hours.

### Other ways to count

- 2,087 hours: some employers, including the US federal government&#x27;s pay system, divide by 2,087, a year of about 52.18 weeks. The answer differs from 2,080 by roughly a third of a percent.
- Unpaid time off: if you take unpaid weeks, use fewer weeks. $60,000 over 50 weeks of 40 hours (2,000 hours) is $30.00 an hour.
- Part-time: use your real hours. A $30,000 salary at 25 hours a week is $30,000 / (25 x 52) = $23.08 an hour.

### Your effective hourly rate

A salary does not rise when you work longer, so extra hours cut your real hourly pay. A $60,000 salary is $28.85 an hour at 40 hours a week but $23.08 at 50 hours: $60,000 / (50 x 52). Use your actual hours when you compare offers.

### Monthly and weekly pay to hourly

Convert to a yearly figure first. A monthly salary times 12 is the annual salary; a weekly pay times 52 is the annual salary; a bi-weekly check times 26 is the annual salary. Then divide by 2,080. A $5,000 monthly salary is $60,000 a year, or $28.85 an hour.

### Try it

The salary to hourly calculator does this for any salary and schedule, and the hourly to salary calculator goes the other way. The salary calculator shows every pay period at once.

### Worked example: comparing two offers

Offer A is a $65,000 salary with an expected 45-hour week. Offer B is $31 an hour for 40 hours, paid for the hours worked. Offer A is $65,000 / (45 x 52) = $65,000 / 2,340 = $27.78 an hour in practice, against $65,000 / 2,080 = $31.25 on paper. Offer B pays $31 x 2,080 = $64,480 a year if you work every week, and extra hours would earn overtime if you are non-exempt. On paper the two look the same; counting the real hours, B pays about $3 more per hour worked. The paper comparison and the real one only agree when the hours do.

### What the 2,080-hour method leaves out

- Benefits. Health insurance, retirement matching and paid leave have value that a plain hourly figure ignores. Compare them separately, in money, before deciding.
- Taxes. Every figure here is gross, before tax. Net pay depends on the country, state, filing status and deductions; see the paycheck calculator for a US estimate.
- Unpaid and paid weeks. If your contract pays for fewer than 52 weeks, divide by the weeks you are actually paid for.
- Commute and unpaid prep time. They are real hours of your life even when they are not paid hours.

### Source

The 2,087-hour divisor used by the US federal government is explained in the Office of Personnel Management fact sheet Computing Hourly Rates of Pay Using the 2087-Hour Divisor. The 2,080-hour figure is plain arithmetic (40 x 52) and is the common private-sector convention, not a legal definition; an employer or a contract may specify a different divisor.


---

# How Overtime Pay Works in the US: Time and a Half Explained

URL: https://calc.streamerosai.com/guides/how-overtime-pay-works/

## How overtime pay works in the US: time and a half explained

Overtime is extra pay for working long weeks. The federal rule is simple to state, but who it covers and how the rate is set is where people get caught out. This guide covers the basics; it is general information, not legal advice.

### The federal rule

Under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), covered non-exempt employees must be paid at least one and a half times their regular rate for each hour worked over 40 in a workweek. A workweek is a fixed, recurring period of seven days, and each week is counted on its own: you cannot average 50 hours one week and 30 the next to avoid overtime.

### How time and a half is calculated

overtime rate = regular rate x 1.5
weekly pay = regular hours x rate + overtime hours x overtime rate At $20 an hour and 45 hours worked, the first 40 hours pay $800 and the 5 overtime hours pay 5 x $30 = $150, for $950 in total. The overtime pay calculator does this with your own rate and hours.

### The "regular rate" is not always your base wage

The regular rate can include more than the hourly wage, such as non-discretionary bonuses and shift differentials. If you receive these, your overtime rate may be higher than 1.5 times your base wage. Check the earnings breakdown on your payslip.

### Exempt and non-exempt employees

Some employees are exempt from the federal overtime rule. Exemption depends on the duties of the job and the salary paid, not on the job title or on being paid a salary. Many salaried workers are non-exempt and are owed overtime. The US Department of Labor publishes the current tests on its website.

### State rules can be stricter

Where state law gives more protection than federal law, the more protective rule applies. California, for example, requires overtime pay for hours over 8 in a day as well as over 40 in a week, and double time after 12 hours in a day. Check your state labor department for the exact rule.

### Holidays and weekends

Federal law does not require a premium for working holidays or weekends. Extra pay for those days comes from an employer&#x27;s policy, a union agreement or a contract. Hours on those days still count toward the 40-hour total. See the time and a half calculator for the rates.

### Worked example: a bonus changes the overtime rate

Suppose you earn $18 an hour, work 45 hours, and are also paid a $90 non-discretionary attendance bonus for the week. The regular rate is all pay for the week divided by all hours worked: ($18 x 45 + $90) / 45 = $900 / 45 = $20.00 an hour, not $18. You have already been paid straight time for all 45 hours, so what is still owed for the 5 overtime hours is the extra half: 0.5 x $20.00 x 5 = $50. The week comes to $900 + $50 = $950. If the bonus were ignored and overtime were figured on $18, the half-time premium would be only 0.5 x $18 x 5 = $45, which is $5 short. Small on one week, but it adds up over a year.

### Worked example: daily overtime in California

A California employee at $20 an hour works five 10-hour days, 50 hours in the week. Each day has 8 regular hours and 2 overtime hours, so 40 regular hours pay $800 and 10 overtime hours pay 10 x $30 = $300, for $1,100. On a single 13-hour day the split is 8 regular hours ($160), 4 hours at 1.5 times ($120) and 1 hour at double time ($40), for $320. The time and a half calculator applies the federal weekly rule and does not model daily overtime, so for California use the arithmetic above.

### Common mistakes

- Averaging weeks. A 50-hour week followed by a 30-hour week is still 10 hours of overtime in the first week.
- Assuming a salary means no overtime. Salary alone does not make someone exempt; the job duties and the salary level both have to meet the Department of Labor tests.
- Counting unpaid breaks. A genuine, uninterrupted meal break is normally not working time, but a break spent answering calls is.
- Forgetting that rates differ. Employers can, and some do, pay more than 1.5 times by contract. The legal minimum is a floor, not a fixed rate.

### Sources and limits

The federal rules come from the Fair Labor Standards Act, summarised by the US Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division in its fact sheet Overtime Pay Requirements of the FLSA (Fact Sheet 23) and, for the regular rate, Fact Sheet 56A, both at dol.gov. California&#x27;s daily rules are described by the state&#x27;s Division of Labor Standards Enforcement at dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_overtime.htm. This page explains the arithmetic. It does not decide whether a particular job is exempt, and it is not legal advice; if pay looks wrong, ask your employer or your state labor department.


---

# How Exchange Rates Work: Mid-Market Rate vs the Rate You Get

URL: https://calc.streamerosai.com/guides/how-exchange-rates-work/

## How exchange rates work: the mid-market rate vs the rate you get

An exchange rate is the price of one currency in another. If 1 US dollar costs 90 Indian rupees, the USD to INR rate is 90. The rate you see on a converter and the rate you are offered when you send money are often not the same number, and the gap is where the cost hides.

### The mid-market rate

In the foreign exchange market every currency pair has a price to buy and a slightly higher price to sell. The mid-market rate is the midpoint between the two. It is the neutral benchmark that converters and news sites show, and it is the fairest number to compare against. The converters on this site use it.

### Why you rarely get it

Banks, card networks, exchange counters and transfer apps make money on currency exchange in two ways, and often both: a margin built into the rate (they sell you a currency for more than the mid-market price) and a separate fee. A transfer that advertises no fee may still be expensive if the margin is large.

### How to compare offers

- Find the mid-market rate for your pair with the currency converter.
- Ask each provider how much the recipient will receive in the end currency after all fees.
- Compare the received amounts, not the headline rate or the fee on its own.
- The difference between the mid-market result and what arrives is your real cost.

### Why rates change

Most major currencies float: their prices move through the day with supply and demand in the market, driven by interest rates, trade, investment flows and news. A few currencies are pegged. The UAE dirham, for example, is held at about 3.6725 to the US dollar, so it moves against other currencies almost exactly as the dollar does.

### Doing the arithmetic yourself

amount in B = amount in A x rate (A to B)
rate (B to A) = 1 / rate (A to B) If 1 euro buys 1.10 dollars, 50 euros is 55 dollars, and 1 dollar buys about 0.909 euros. See the converter for a live example, or open a popular pair such as USD to INR.

### Worked example: what a transfer really costs

Say you want to send $1,000 to India and the mid-market rate is 90 rupees to the dollar, so the benchmark outcome is 90,000 rupees. The two providers below use made-up numbers to show the method; they are not real quotes.
Provider Fee Rate offered Rupees received Cost against 90,000
A: fee shown, wide margin $5 88.20 (1,000 - 5) x 88.20 = 87,759 2,241 (2.49%)
B: no fee, narrow margin $0 89.55 1,000 x 89.55 = 89,550 450 (0.50%)
Provider A looks fine if you only look at its $5 fee, but its rate is 2% below the mid-market rate, so it costs about five times as much overall. The percentage cost is (mid-market result - amount received) / mid-market result.

### Paying by card abroad

When a card terminal or a website offers to charge you in your home currency instead of the local one (often called dynamic currency conversion), the shop or its processor sets the rate, and it is commonly worse than the rate your card network would apply. Choosing the local currency usually gives a better rate, though your own bank may still add a foreign transaction fee. Check your card terms for that fee.

### Where the rates on this site come from

The converters load daily rates from free public rate feeds (an open currency API and exchangerate-api.com, with a fallback between them) in your browser. They are reference rates for planning, in the same spirit as the mid-market rate, but they are not a quote: a bank, card or transfer provider will give you a different number, and rates for smaller currencies may be updated less often than for the major ones. Do not use this page to settle a contract or a trade; ask the provider for a firm quote.

# About StreamerOS Money Calculators: Free, Private Money Math

URL: https://calc.streamerosai.com/about/

## About

StreamerOS Money Calculators is a small set of free calculators for everyday money questions: pay raises, salary and hourly conversion, overtime and time and a half, and currency conversion between any two currencies, with short guides that explain the rules behind them.
It is built and maintained by Yaseen Khatib, a full-stack AI engineer, as part of the StreamerOS project. The calculators exist because many are cluttered and never show how the answer is reached, so every page here states its formula and a worked example.

### How the calculators work

Every calculator runs in your browser using standard JavaScript. The figures you enter are processed on your device and are not sent to a server or stored. The currency tools download a public list of exchange rates; your amounts are never part of that request. The site is a static website hosted on GitHub Pages.

### What the results are, and are not

Pay results are estimates of gross pay before tax and other deductions. Currency results use mid-market reference rates from a free public feed, which can be up to a day old and are not the rate a bank or transfer service will give you. None of it is financial, tax or legal advice. Overtime rules in particular vary by state and by job, so check your payslip or your state labor department for the exact rule that applies to you.

### Who is behind it

The site is run by one person, Yaseen Khatib, a full-stack AI developer based in Hyderabad, India. His portfolio is at yk.streamerosai.com. There is no team and no company behind the pages, which is why corrections go straight to him through the contact page. The same family of small sites also includes tools for developers, money, images and maths at tools, calc, images and math on streamerosai.com.

### How pages are kept accurate

The calculation code has automated tests, every formula is written out on the page with a worked example you can check by hand, and facts that come from outside (rates, rules, standards) name their source. Each page shows the date it was last reviewed, and that date changes only when the page does. The assumptions and limits of a tool are stated on its page rather than hidden, and a result that cannot be right (an impossible date, for instance) shows a message instead of a number. The terms of use and privacy policy describe the rest.

### How the site is funded

The calculators are free. The site does not show ads at the moment; it may show Google AdSense ads to cover hosting and development time. Ads never change the result of a calculator.

### Corrections

If a result is wrong or a guide contains a mistake, please use the contact page. Fixes are made in the open and the guides are updated.

# Privacy Policy: StreamerOS Money Calculators

URL: https://calc.streamerosai.com/privacy/

## Privacy Policy

This policy describes what StreamerOS Money Calculators ( https://calc.streamerosai.com) does with information when you use it. Last updated: 19 November 2026.

### What the tools do with your input

The calculators work entirely in your browser. The pay figures and amounts you type are not transmitted to our servers, logged, or stored. Closing the page clears them.
The currency tools request a public list of exchange rates from jsDelivr, Cloudflare Pages or ExchangeRate-API when you open them. That request does not contain your amounts, but, as with any website you visit, those services can see your IP address.

### Cookies and similar technologies

Cookies are small files a site stores in your browser. The analytics and advertising services listed below may set cookies or read similar identifiers. The tools themselves do not need a cookie to work. The only thing the site stores for its own use is your light or dark theme choice, kept in your browser&#x27;s local storage and never sent anywhere. You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings; the tools keep working either way.

### Analytics

This site uses Google Analytics 4 to count visits and see which pages are useful. It collects page views, approximate location, device and browser type, and how you arrived, using cookies and similar identifiers. It does not receive the text you enter into the tools. You can opt out with the Google Analytics opt-out browser add-on. We do not sell personal information.

### Usage recording

This site uses Microsoft Clarity to see how pages are used, through heatmaps and anonymised session recordings (mouse movement, clicks and scrolling). Clarity is configured to mask the text on the page, so what you type or load into a tool is not recorded. Clarity sets its own cookies ( _clck, _clsk) and Microsoft cookies on clarity.ms and bing.com (such as MUID); see Microsoft&#x27;s privacy statement.

### First-party visit counter

The site also runs a small counter of its own, Pulse, a script served from our own Cloudflare Worker (pulse.yaseenyk.workers.dev), to tell real visits from automated ones. It records the page address (without the query string), the referring site and campaign tags, country, device type, browser and system name, screen size, language, the name of your network provider, scroll depth, time on the page, page speed, which links and buttons were clicked, and a human-or-bot signal. It sets no cookies, never reads what you type or the values in input fields, and stores no IP address or browser string: the address is used in memory only, to limit abuse and to make a visitor code that changes every day (a one-way hash with a random salt that is deleted the next day), so visits cannot be linked across days. Records are deleted after 90 days. It switches itself off when your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control, and on localhost. The data is used only to understand how the site is used.

### Advertising

This site does not show ads at the moment. We intend to use Google AdSense after approval. Once ads run, Google and its partners may use cookies to serve ads based on your visits to this and other websites. You can opt out of personalised advertising at adssettings.google.com, and learn how Google uses data from sites that use its services at policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites. Where required by law (for example in the EEA and UK), personalised ads will be shown only after you consent. Ads will never change a tool&#x27;s result, and this policy will be updated before ads go live if anything above changes.

### Your choices

You can use the site with cookies blocked, opt out of Google Analytics with the add-on above, turn on Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control to switch off the visit counter, and ask a privacy question through the contact page. We do not collect accounts, names or email addresses through the tools. If you write to us, we use your address only to reply.

### Children

The tools are general-purpose and not aimed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data.

### Contact

Questions about this policy: see the contact page. The rules for using the site are in the terms of use.
